options.text: endpoint detection and response (EDR) in block mode

questions.explanation:
Custom network indicators enables creation of custom allow or block indicators for IP addresses, URLs, and domains in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Microsoft documents this feature as the Advanced features setting required before blocking IP addresses or URLs. Custom indicators support individual external IP addresses rather than IP ranges.

**Learn more:** [Create indicators for IPs and URLs/domains](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/indicator-ip-domain) · [Configure advanced features in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/advanced-features)

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a database server named DB1. DB1 is onboarded to Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
You need to ensure that DB1 is shown on the attack surface map.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Security Exposure Management uses critical asset classification to identify and prioritize business-critical devices, including databases. Critical assets are surfaced in the attack surface map with criticality indicators; a critical asset rule can classify DB1 as such.

**Learn more:** [Get started with Microsoft Security Exposure Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security-exposure-management/get-started-exposure-management) · [Overview of critical asset management in Microsoft Security Exposure Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security-exposure-management/critical-asset-management)

You have Microsoft SharePoint Online sites containing sensitive documents. The documents contain customer account numbers, each consisting of 32 alphanumeric characters.  
  
You need to create a data loss prevention (DLP) policy to protect the sensitive documents.  
  
What should you use to identify which documents are sensitive?

options.text: a hunting query in Microsoft 365 Defender

questions.explanation:
A regular expression can define a custom sensitive information type that detects strings matching the required 32-character alphanumeric account-number format. Microsoft Purview DLP uses regular expressions to identify and classify sensitive-data patterns in content.

**Learn more:** [Learn about using regular expressions (regex) in data loss prevention policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-policy-learn-about-regex-use) · [Learn about sensitive information types](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sit-sensitive-information-type-learn-about)

In the Microsoft Defender portal, you discover that an alert was triggered for Device1.

options.text: Initiate an automated investigation and view the results in the Action center.

questions.explanation: Microsoft Sentinel automation rules and playbooks together minimize administrative effort for incident response. Automation rules automatically execute when incidents are created or updated, performing actions like status changes, owner assignment, and tag management. Playbooks (based on Azure Logic Apps) provide powerful remediation capabilities, often triggered by automation rules. Workbooks, Azure Automation runbooks, and Azure Functions are not designed for automated incident handling.

options.text: Collect the Microsoft Defender Antivirus troubleshooting diagnostic files.

questions.explanation:

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your on-premises network has two Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domains named contoso.com and fabrikam.com. Contoso.com has a group named Group1. Fabrikam.com has a group named Group2.  
  
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named WS1 that contains a scheduled query rule named Rule1. Rule1 creates alerts in response to anomalous AD DS security events. Every alert creates an incident.  
  
You need to implement an incident-triage solution that meets the following requirements:  
  
- Security incidents from contoso.com must be assigned to Group1.  
- Security incidents from fabrikam.com must be assigned to Group2.  
- Administrative effort must be minimized.  
  
What should you include in the solution?

options.text: a playbook that is triggered by the creation of an incident
a playbook that is triggered by the creation of an alert
one automation rule assigned to Rule1
two automation rules assigned to Rule1

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel automation rules can automatically perform incident triage actions, including assigning an incident owner. Because each assignment action targets a single group, create one Rule1-scoped automation rule for contoso.com incidents that assigns Group1, and another for fabrikam.com incidents that assigns Group2. This uses built-in incident automation and avoids the extra administration of playbooks.

**Learn more:** [Create and use Microsoft Sentinel automation rules to manage response](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-manage-use-automation-rules) · [Scheduled analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/scheduled-rules-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a Microsoft Sentinel workspace and a virtual machine named VM1. VM1 runs Linux and hosts a log forwarder that receives Syslog and Common Event Format (CEF) messages from network appliances on TCP/UDP port 514. VM1 has the Azure Monitor Agent installed and is associated with one data collection rule (DCR) that collects Syslog facilities.  
  
You find that when the appliances send CEF messages by using the `local0` facility, the events are ingested into both the `CommonSecurityLog` table and the `Syslog` table.  
  
You need to prevent the CEF messages from being ingested into the `Syslog` table. The solution must ensure that the CEF messages continue to be ingested into `CommonSecurityLog`.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: an analytics rule in Microsoft Sentinel

questions.explanation:
An ingestion-time transformation on the Syslog stream can filter out CEF-formatted messages before they are written to the Syslog table, while the separate CEF stream continues to write those events to CommonSecurityLog. Microsoft documents this as the approach to avoid duplication when Syslog and CEF use the same facility.

**Learn more:** [Syslog and Common Event Format (CEF) via AMA connectors for Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/cef-syslog-ama-overview) · [Ingest syslog and CEF messages to Microsoft Sentinel with the Azure Monitor Agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/connect-cef-syslog-ama?tabs=syslog%2Cportal)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription with Azure Defender enabled for every supported resource type.  
  
You need to configure continuous export of high-severity alerts so that a third-party security information and event management (SIEM) solution can retrieve them.  
  
To which service should the alerts be exported?
questions.explanation:
Azure Event Hubs is the continuous-export destination for streaming Microsoft Defender for Cloud alerts to downstream consumers such as third-party SIEM solutions. Continuous export supports filtering alert data by severity, including high-severity alerts.

**Learn more:** [Set up continuous export in the Azure portal - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/continuous-export) · [Stream alerts to monitoring solutions - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/export-to-siem)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must implement the Azure Information Protection requirements.  
  
What should you configure first?

options.text: Device health and compliance reports settings in Microsoft Defender Security Center
scanner clusters in Azure Information Protection from the Azure portal
content scan jobs in Azure Information Protection from the Azure portal
Advanced features from Settings in Microsoft Defender Security Center

questions.explanation:
The legacy Azure Information Protection integration with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint is enabled from **Settings > Advanced features** in Microsoft Defender Security Center. Enabling it allows Defender for Endpoint to discover labeled files on Windows endpoints and send the associated data to Azure Information Protection. Scanner clusters and content scan jobs are for scanning on-premises repositories and are not the prerequisite for endpoint integration.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender ATP integrates with Microsoft Information Protection](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2019/01/17/windows-defender-atp-integrates-with-microsoft-information-protection-to-discover-protect-and-monitor-sensitive-data-on-windows-devices/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have three Azure subscriptions, each containing multiple virtual machines running Windows Server.  
  
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.  
  
You need to ensure that failed sign-in attempts from every virtual machine can be analyzed by using Microsoft Sentinel. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From the Microsoft Defender portal, install the Windows Security Events solution.
On each virtual machine, create an event subscription.
On each virtual machine, install the Azure Connected Machine agent.
From the Microsoft Defender portal, install the Syslog solution.

questions.explanation:
The Windows Security Events solution enables the Microsoft Sentinel Windows Security Events connector, which collects Windows Security event logs such as failed logon events. Its Azure Monitor Agent-based collection can be managed at scale through data collection rules, reducing per-VM administration. Azure Arc/Connected Machine agent is required for non-Azure machines, not Azure virtual machines.

**Learn more:** [Connect Microsoft Sentinel to other Microsoft services with a Windows agent-based data connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/connect-services-windows-based) · [Collect Windows events from virtual machines with Azure Monitor Agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/vm/data-collection-windows-events)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace that includes Common Event Format (CEF) data.  
  
You need to run a query on the CEF data.  
  
Which table should you query?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel collects Common Event Format (CEF) events in the CommonSecurityLog table, including events sent from security appliances such as Check Point and Palo Alto.\
\
**Learn more:** [CommonSecurityLog table reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/tables/commonsecuritylog) · [CEF and CommonSecurityLog field mapping](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/cef-name-mapping)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2. The subscription includes 1,000 Windows 11 devices running third-party antivirus software with Smart App Control enabled.  
  
You need to ensure that, if Defender for Endpoint detects a malicious artifact missed by the third-party software, it automatically remediates that artifact.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: endpoint detection and response (EDR) in block mode

questions.explanation:
Endpoint detection and response (EDR) in block mode provides post-breach protection for devices that use a non-Microsoft antivirus solution while Microsoft Defender Antivirus runs in passive mode. It blocks and automatically remediates malicious artifacts detected by Defender for Endpoint that the primary antivirus product missed.

**Learn more:** [Endpoint detection and response in block mode - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 1,000 on-premises Windows 11 Pro devices that are onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
You discover that an attacker performed the following actions on a device:  
  
- Modified the file system path of a registry-based antivirus exclusion  
- Downloaded a malicious file to that file system path  
  
You initiate a live response session on the device.  
  
You need to remove the malicious file.  
  
Which command should you run?
questions.explanation:
In Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Live Response, `remediate` removes an entity from a device. For a file entity, the remediation action is deletion, so it removes the malicious file at the specified path.

**Learn more:** [Live response command examples - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/live-response-command-examples) · [Investigate entities on devices using live response in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/defender-endpoint/live-response)

questions.question:

You need to enable just-in-time (JIT) VM access and network detections for Azure resources. Where should Azure Defender be enabled?

questions.question:

You need to ensure that particular Defender for Cloud security alerts are suppressed at the root management group level. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do in the Azure portal?

options.text: Modify the Workload protections settings in Defender for Cloud.

questions.question:

questions.question: Which team’s issue can be addressed by using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint delivers endpoint threat protection, detection, investigation, and response for organizational devices. This addresses the security risks of a sales team’s portable and remotely used endpoints.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender for Endpoint overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/microsoft-defender-endpoint)

questions.question: Which team’s issue can be addressed by using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint?
questions.explanation:
The ASR rule identified by `D4F940AB-401B-4EFC-AADC-AD5F3C50688A` blocks Office applications from creating child processes, including malicious VBA macro activity that downloads and attempts to run additional payloads. The rule must use the `Enabled` action; `AuditMode` only records the activity without blocking it. Both `Add-MpPreference` and `Set-MpPreference` can enable the rule, although `Set-MpPreference` replaces existing ASR-rule settings.

**Learn more:** [ASR rules reference - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference) · [Add-MpPreference (Defender)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-au/powershell/module/defender/add-mppreference?view=windowsserver2022-ps)

You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.  
  
You enable User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) by using Audit Logs and Signin Logs.  
  
The following entities are identified in the Azure AD tenant:  
  
- App name: App1  
- IP address: 192.168.1.2  
- Computer name: Device1  
- Used client app: Microsoft Edge  
- Email address: [email protected]  
- Sign-in URL: https://www.company.com  
  
Which entities can be investigated by using UEBA?

options.text: IP address and email address only
app name, computer name, IP address, email address, and used client app only
used client app and app name only

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel UEBA uses connected Audit Logs and Signin Logs to build behavioral context for users, devices or hosts, IP addresses, and applications. The email address represents a user identity, the computer name represents a device, and the app name and client app provide application-related activity context. A sign-in URL is not an investigable UEBA entity in this scenario.

**Learn more:** [Enable User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/enable-entity-behavior-analytics) · [Microsoft Sentinel User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/ueba-reference)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains a user named User1 and a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named WS1. WS1 uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
You have the Microsoft security analytics rules shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783739295356-zn6cocbt.png)  
  
User1 performs an action that matches Rule1, Rule2, Rule3, and Rule4.  
  
How many incidents will be created in WS1?
questions.explanation: Each analytics rule configured to create an incident does so independently whenever its own criteria are met; alerts are not automatically merged across separate rules unless explicit cross-rule incident grouping or automation is configured. Because the single action satisfies the criteria of all four distinct rules, each rule fires and produces its own incident, resulting in four incidents in WS1.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR and contains a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can manage Microsoft Defender XDR custom detection rules and Endpoint security policies. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation: The **Security Administrator** role has permissions to manage both custom detection rules and endpoint security policies in Microsoft Defender XDR. The Security Operator role can view and manage alerts but cannot modify policies. Following least privilege, the minimum role that grants both required permissions is Security Administrator.

questions.question:
You have 50 Microsoft Sentinel workspaces.  
  
You need to view every incident from all the workspaces on one page in the Azure portal. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
Which Azure portal page should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Sentinel landing page lets you select multiple accessible workspaces and open a unified incident view. Multiple workspace view supports up to 100 workspaces and displays incidents from the selected workspaces in one list, so it accommodates 50 workspaces without building a separate aggregation solution.\
\
**Learn more:** [Work with Microsoft Sentinel incidents in many workspaces at once](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/multiple-workspace-view)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR. All endpoint devices are onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
You have an Azure subscription containing a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named Workspace1. All Microsoft Defender XDR events are ingested into Workspace1.  
  
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You create a KQL query named query1 that searches device logs for a known vulnerability.  
  
You need to ensure that query1 runs every hour. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender XDR custom detection rules use advanced hunting KQL queries and can run at a configured frequency, including every hour. Configuring query1 as a custom detection rule therefore schedules the recurring vulnerability search with minimal administration.

**Learn more:** [Create custom detection rules in Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/custom-detection-rules)

questions.question:
You need to recommend a solution that satisfies the technical requirements for the Azure virtual machines.  
  
What should the recommendation include?
questions.explanation:
Azure Defender, now delivered through Microsoft Defender for Cloud/Defender for Servers, provides security protection for Azure virtual machines, including threat detection and VM security controls. Just-in-time VM access is a capability provided through Defender for Cloud rather than a substitute for the broader VM protection service.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable Just-in-Time Access - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/enable-just-in-time-access) · [Protect your Virtual Machines (VMs) with Microsoft Defender for Servers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/tutorial-protect-resources)

questions.question:
Solution: You create a scheduled query rule for a data connector.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel scheduled analytics rules run KQL queries against data ingested through connectors. When the query detects the defined malicious-IP sign-in condition, the rule generates an alert; incident creation is enabled by default for alerts generated by the rule.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create scheduled analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-analytics-rules) · [Scheduled analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/scheduled-rules-overview)

questions.question:
Solution: You create a hunting bookmark.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
A hunting bookmark records selected hunting results for later investigation. It does not automatically detect sign-ins from malicious IP addresses or create incidents. Automated incident generation is configured through an analytics rule with incident creation enabled.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create scheduled analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-analytics-rules) · [Keep track of data during hunting with Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/bookmarks)

questions.question:
Solution: You create a Microsoft incident-creation rule for a data connector.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation: A Microsoft incident creation rule only converts alerts that a connected Microsoft security product (such as Defender for Cloud or Defender for Identity) has already generated into Sentinel incidents; it does not itself inspect raw sign-in or activity data for indicators like a malicious source IP address. Detecting a sign-in to an Azure VM from a malicious IP requires a custom (scheduled) or Fusion analytics rule that queries the relevant logs and correlates them against threat-intelligence indicators, so enabling an incident creation rule alone does not meet this goal.

questions.question:
Solution: You create a livestream based on a query.  
  
Does this fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel hunting livestreams run queries interactively and notify on matches, but they do not automatically create incidents. An analytics rule is required to detect the malicious sign-in and generate the associated alert and incident.\
\
**Learn more:** [Detect threats by using hunting livestream in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/livestream)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
You are investigating an incident.  
  
You need to review the incident tasks that have been performed.  
  
What can you use on the Incident page?

options.text: Tasks, Activity log, and Alert timeline

questions.explanation:
The Incident page provides tasks for tracking investigation work, an activity log for reviewing actions taken on the incident, and an alert timeline that shows the related alerts in chronological order.\
\
**Learn more:** [Investigate incidents in the Microsoft Defender portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/investigate-incidents) · [Manage incidents in Microsoft Defender](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/manage-incidents)

questions.question:
You have 500 on-premises Windows 11 devices that use Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  

You enable Network device discovery.  
  
You need to create a hunting query that will identify discovered network devices and return the identity of the onboarded device that discovered each network device.  
  
Which built-in function should you use?
questions.explanation: The SeenBy() built-in function is essential for network device discovery queries. It returns details on which onboarded device observed each discovered network device, helping locate devices in the network topology. DeviceFromIP(), next(), and current_cluster_endpoint() do not provide the device-to-device visibility needed for this hunting scenario.

questions.question:
You have 500 on-premises Windows 11 devices that use Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  

You enable Network device discovery.  
  
You need to create a hunting query that will identify discovered network devices and return the identity of the onboarded device that discovered each network device.  
  
Which built-in function should you use?

options.text: From the History tab in the Action center, revert the actions.
From the investigation page, review the AIR processes.
From Quarantine from the Review page, modify the rules.
From Threat tracker, review the queries.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender’s Action center History tab records completed remediation actions and lets authorized users undo a **Quarantine file** action. For a file quarantined on multiple devices, the undo operation can be applied to the additional instances, releasing the file from quarantine.

**Learn more:** [View and manage actions in the Action center — Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/m365d-autoir-actions)

questions.question:
You have a custom Microsoft Sentinel workbook named Workbook1.  
  
You need to add a grid to Workbook1. The solution must ensure that the grid includes a maximum of 100 rows.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: In the grid query, include the take operator.
In the grid query, include the project operator.
In the query editor interface, configure Settings.
In the query editor interface, select Advanced Editor.

questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor workbook grids have a configurable row limit in the query component’s advanced settings. Configure the grid-row limit as 100 to ensure that no more than 100 rows are displayed.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Workbooks data source limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/visualize/workbooks-limits)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named WS1 and 100 virtual machines that run Windows Server.  
  
You need to configure the collection of Windows Security event logs for ingestion to WS1. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
• Capture a full user audit trail including user sign-in and user sign-out events.  

• Minimize the volume of events.  

• Minimize administrative effort.  
  
Which event set should you select?
questions.explanation: The **Common** event set is a predefined collection of Windows Security events that includes sign-in (4624) and sign-out (4634) events, providing a full user audit trail. It strikes a balance between capturing necessary audit information and minimizing event volume compared to \"All events.\" It requires no custom configuration, minimizing administrative effort.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Copilot for Security.  
  
You plan to run the following code to create a custom Copilot for Security plugin.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783741535097-laki34qn.png)  
  
You need to specify a format and complete the code segment.  
  
Which format should you use for the   

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783741538748-mydk6e3h.png)  

variable?
questions.explanation: Custom Copilot for Security plugins use KQL (Kusto Query Language) as the format for specifying queries and operations. KQL is the native query language for Microsoft security products and Defender for Endpoint.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Copilot for Security.  
  
You plan to run the following code to create a custom Copilot for Security plugin.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783741535097-laki34qn.png)

Which format should you use for the

variable?

options.text: a URL/domain indicator that has Action set to Alert only
a URL/domain indicator that has Action set to Alert and block
a file hash indicator that has Action set to Alert and block
a certificate indicator that has Action set to Alert and block

questions.explanation:
A file hash indicator identifies the malicious image file itself and can be configured to raise an alert and block the file when a device attempts to run it. URL/domain indicators manage web access, and certificate indicators apply to signed files associated with a certificate rather than the specific malicious file.

**Learn more:** [Create indicators for files - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/indicator-file)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and contains the devices shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783741310705-8gcu52cy.png)  
  
You initiate a live response session on each device.  
  
You need to collect a Defender for Endpoint investigation package from each device.  
  
On which devices can you collect the package by running advanced live response commands from the command-line interface (CLI)?
questions.explanation: The collect command for gathering forensics packages via live response CLI is supported only on macOS and Linux devices (Device3 and Device4). Windows devices (Device1 and Device2) do not support this advanced command in live response sessions. This limitation is documented in the Defender for Endpoint live response command reference.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Windows device named Device1 that is onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
You create an attack surface reduction (ASR) policy named Policy1 and configure **Block all Office applications from creating child processes** as **Block**.  
  
On Device1, a required Microsoft Office plugin named Plugin1 fails.  
  
You need to validate whether Policy1 is causing Plugin1 to fail on Device1. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From the Microsoft Defender portal, enable Selective isolation mode for Device1.
From the Microsoft Defender portal, enable troubleshooting mode for Device1.
On Device1, run the Set-MpPreference -DisableTamperProtection $true cmdlet.
On Device1, run the Set-MpPreference -AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Ids E5AF940AB-401D-41FC-AADC-AD5F3C50679AAttackSurfaceReductionRules_Actions cmdlet.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint troubleshooting mode temporarily allows local administrators to modify policy-managed Microsoft Defender Antivirus settings on a specific device for compatibility testing. Microsoft’s documented scenario for an Office plugin blocked by the ASR rule **Block all Office applications from creating child processes** begins by enabling troubleshooting mode, after which the ASR rule can be temporarily disabled to confirm whether the plugin works.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshooting mode scenarios in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/troubleshooting-mode-scenarios) · [Get started with troubleshooting mode in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-troubleshooting-mode)

questions.question:
You need to finish the query for failed sign-ins to meet the technical requirements.  
  
Where can you locate the column name needed to complete the `where` clause?

options.text: Security alerts in Azure Security Center
the query windows of the Log Analytics workspace

questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor Log Analytics displays tables and their columns in its schema pane within the query interface. Those column names are used when writing Kusto Query Language `where` clauses.\
\
**Learn more:** [Get started with log queries in Azure Monitor Logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/get-started-queries)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named Workspace1.  
  
In Workspace1, you create a Microsoft Sentinel workbook called WB1.  
  
You need to add a query to WB1 that returns a list of every watchlist in Workspace1.  
  
What should you set as the query’s **Data source**?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel provides the `_GetWatchlistAlias` KQL function to return the aliases of all watchlists in a workspace. KQL queries against the workspace are run through the Logs (Analytics) workbook data source.\
\
**Learn more:** [Build queries or rules with watchlists - Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/watchlists-queries) · [Use watchlists to correlate and enrich event data in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/watchlists)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to use PowerShell on a Windows device to search the Microsoft Purview audit log.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Install the Microsoft Graph PowerShell module.
Install the Microsoft Exchange Online PowerShell module.

questions.explanation:
The `Search-UnifiedAuditLog` cmdlet used to search the Microsoft Purview unified audit log is provided by Exchange Online PowerShell. Installing the Exchange Online PowerShell module is therefore the required first step.\
\
**Learn more:** [Search-UnifiedAuditLog (ExchangePowerShell)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/search-unifiedauditlog?view=exchange-ps) · [Use a PowerShell script to search the audit log](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-log-search-script)

options.text: From Azure Security Center, enable workflow automation.
Create an Azure logic app that has a manual trigger.
Create an Azure logic app that has an Azure Security Center alert trigger.
Create an Azure logic app that has an HTTP trigger.
From Azure Active Directory (Azure AD), add an app registration.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud workflow automation can automatically invoke a Logic App when a security alert meets configured criteria. The Logic App must use the Microsoft Defender for Cloud (Azure Security Center) alert trigger so it receives the alert event, and workflow automation must be enabled to run it automatically.

**Learn more:** [Workflow automation — Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/workflow-automations) · [Microsoft Defender for Cloud Alert connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/ascalert/)

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription using Microsoft Copilot for Security. Copilot for Security is configured with its default settings.  
  
You need to ensure that a user named User can use Copilot for Security to perform the following tasks:  
  
- Upload files.  
- View the usage dashboard.  
- Share promptbooks with all users.  
  
The solution must adhere to the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User?
questions.explanation:
The Copilot owner role permits file uploads, viewing the Security Copilot usage dashboard, and sharing promptbooks with the tenant. Although a Copilot contributor can upload files and share promptbooks under default settings, contributors cannot view the usage dashboard. Copilot owner is therefore the minimum role that grants every required capability.

**Learn more:** [Understand authentication in Microsoft Security Copilot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/security/authentication) · [Manage security compute unit usage in Security Copilot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/security/manage-usage)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription using Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 1 that contains a server named Server1.  
  
You enable agentless scanning.  
  
You need to stop Server1 from being scanned while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Upgrade the subscription to Defender for Servers Plan 2.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud can exclude individual machines from agentless scanning by matching a configured exclusion tag (name/value pair) applied to the resource; tagged machines are skipped on the next discovery cycle. Applying a single tag to Server1 is far less effort than upgrading the subscription plan, building a governance rule, or creating an exclusion group, none of which is the mechanism used to opt specific machines out of agentless scanning.

**Learn more:** [Exclude machines from agentless scanning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/exclude-machines-agentless-scanning)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that includes a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.  
  
You need to create a playbook that runs automatically in response to a Microsoft Sentinel alert.  
  
What should you create first?

options.text: a hunting query in Microsoft Sentinel
an automation rule in Microsoft Sentinel

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel playbooks are workflows built in Azure Logic Apps. An automation rule can subsequently associate an alert-triggered response with the playbook, but the Logic App that implements the playbook must exist first.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Logic Apps for Microsoft Sentinel playbooks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/logic-apps-playbooks) · [Create and manage Microsoft Sentinel playbooks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/create-playbooks)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that includes a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.  
  
You need to create a playbook that runs automatically in response to a Microsoft Sentinel alert.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation:
Deploying and customizing Microsoft Sentinel workbook templates requires the Microsoft.Insights/workbooktemplates write/delete/read permissions, which are granted by the Azure Monitor built-in Workbook Contributor role. Microsoft Sentinel Contributor manages workbook instances but not templates, so Workbook Contributor is the least-privileged role that meets the requirement.

**Learn more:** [Azure built-in roles - Workbook Contributor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/monitor#workbook-contributor)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
You are investigating an attacker that is known to use the Microsoft Graph API as an attack vector. The attacker performs the tactics shown the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783740192955-60aqo9bb.png)  
  
You need to search for malicious activities in your organization.  
  
Which tactics can you analyze by using the MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs table?
questions.explanation: While the consensus indicates all three tactics can be analyzed via MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs, Tactic3 (Azure virtual machine deletion) is primarily an Azure Resource Manager (ARM) operation, not a Microsoft Graph API operation, and would be logged in AzureActivity logs instead. Tactic1 (mailbox reconnaissance) and Tactic2 (Teams chat access) are definitely Graph API activities. The consensus may reflect incomplete understanding of which API each tactic uses.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
You need to create a query to link the AlertInfo, AlertEvidence, and DeviceLogonEvents tables. The solution must return every row from the tables.  
  
Which operator should you use?
questions.explanation:
The KQL `search *` operator searches all tables in scope with a wildcard predicate that is equivalent to an always-true condition, returning every row and identifying the source table in the results. An inner join returns only rows with matching join keys, while an inner union limits output columns to those shared by all inputs.

**Learn more:** [search operator - Kusto](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/kusto/query/search-operator?view=microsoft-fabric) · [Learn the advanced hunting query language in Microsoft Defender](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-query-language)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Sentinel deployment in the East US Azure region.  
  
You create a Log Analytics workspace named LogsWest in the West US Azure region.  
  
You need to ensure that scheduled analytics rules in the existing Azure Sentinel deployment can generate alerts from queries against LogsWest.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Deploy Azure Data Catalog to the West US Azure region.
Modify the workspace settings of the existing Azure Sentinel deployment.
Add Azure Sentinel to a workspace.
Create a data connector in Azure Sentinel.

questions.explanation:
Cross-workspace scheduled analytics rules can query another Log Analytics workspace only when Microsoft Sentinel is deployed on every workspace referenced by the query. Enabling Azure Sentinel on LogsWest satisfies that prerequisite; alerts generated by the rule remain in the workspace where the rule is defined.

**Learn more:** [Extend Microsoft Sentinel across workspaces and tenants](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/extend-sentinel-across-workspaces-tenants)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named Workspace1 and a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can investigate incidents by using Workspace1. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft's own prerequisites for incident investigation state that a Microsoft Sentinel Responder role assignment is required to investigate incidents, since it allows viewing incident details, updating status, and adding comments. Sentinel Reader is read-only and cannot interact with an incident, while Contributor and Automation Contributor grant broader configuration rights than needed.

**Learn more:** [Investigate incidents with Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/investigate-incidents)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a third-party security information and event management (SIEM) solution.  
  
You need to make sure that the SIEM solution can generate alerts for Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) sign-in events in near real time.  
  
What should you do to route events to the SIEM solution?

options.text: Create an Azure Sentinel workspace that has a Security Events connector.
Configure the Diagnostics settings in Azure AD to stream to an event hub.
Create an Azure Sentinel workspace that has an Azure Active Directory connector.
Configure the Diagnostics settings in Azure AD to archive to a storage account.

questions.explanation:
Azure AD diagnostic settings can stream selected sign-in log categories to an Azure Event Hub. Event Hubs is the supported route for integrating Microsoft Entra ID activity logs with third-party SIEM tools, enabling the SIEM to ingest and analyze the events. Archiving to Storage is for retention, and Sentinel connectors apply to Microsoft Sentinel rather than an external SIEM.

**Learn more:** [Stream Microsoft Entra logs to an event hub](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-stream-logs-to-event-hub) · [Access activity logs in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-access-activity-logs)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes two users, User1 and User2, and uses Microsoft Copilot for Security.  
  
From the Copilot for Security portal, User1 begins a session and creates these prompts:  
  
- Prompt1: Provides access to the Entra plugin  
- Prompt2: Provides access to the Intune plugin  
- Prompt3: Provides access to the Entra plugin  
  
User1 shares the session with User2.  
  
User2 does **NOT** have access to Microsoft Intune.  
  
For which prompts can User2 view results in the shared session?
questions.explanation:
Shared Microsoft Security Copilot sessions contain all prompts and responses and are displayed statically to authorized recipients. Access to a plugin’s underlying service and data is required to generate a response, but it is not reevaluated when a recipient views a shared session. A recipient without Intune access can therefore still view results generated through the Intune plugin, as well as results from the Entra plugin.

**Learn more:** [Understand authentication in Microsoft Security Copilot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/security/authentication)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Copilot for Security.  
  
You have a Copilot for Security workspace that uses the following plugins:  
  
- Microsoft Entra  
- Microsoft Defender XDR  
  
From the Microsoft Defender portal, you use Copilot for Security to investigate a reported incident.  
  
You need to run a promptbook that includes information from Microsoft Entra ID Protection in the investigation.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From the Microsoft Defender portal, create an incident report.
Open the investigation in the Copilot for Security standalone experience.
Open the investigation in Microsoft Sentinel.
From the Microsoft Defender portal, create an advanced hunting query.

questions.explanation:
The standalone Microsoft Security Copilot experience provides access to the promptbook library and to additional enabled plugins. Opening the Defender investigation in that experience allows the Microsoft Entra plugin to supply Microsoft Entra ID Protection information while the promptbook runs.

**Learn more:** [Use promptbooks in Microsoft Security Copilot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/security/using-promptbooks) · [Security Copilot in Microsoft Entra](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/security-copilot/security-copilot-in-entra)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 500 on-premises devices.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender 365.  
  
You onboard 100 devices to Microsoft Defender 365.  
  
You need to identify any unmanaged on-premises devices. The solution must ensure that only specific onboarded devices perform the discovery.  
  
What should you do first?
questions.explanation:
Device discovery lets you control which onboarded devices act as discovery sensors by assigning them a device tag and then restricting standard discovery to devices carrying that tag; untagged devices fall back to basic discovery only. Device groups are used for RBAC and policy targeting rather than selecting discovery sensors, and neither the discovery mode setting nor exclusions let you designate specific devices as the ones performing the scan.

**Learn more:** [Device discovery frequently asked questions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/device-discovery-faq)

questions.question:
You need to remediate ongoing attacks to satisfy the technical requirements.  
  
What should you include in the solution?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel playbooks are Azure Logic Apps workflows that automate and orchestrate threat-response and remediation actions. They can run automatically in response to configured alerts or incidents, enabling rapid remediation of active attacks.\
\
**Learn more:** [Automate threat response with playbooks in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/automate-responses-with-playbooks)

You have the following advanced hunting query in Microsoft 365 Defender.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783728840163-z82aewjj.png)  
  
You must receive an alert when any process disables System Restore on a device managed by Microsoft Defender during the past 24 hours.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Add | order by Timestamp to the query.
Add DeviceId and ReportId to the output of the query.

questions.explanation:
A custom detection rule turns matching advanced-hunting results into alerts. For Microsoft Defender for Endpoint event tables such as DeviceProcessEvents, the query results must contain Timestamp, DeviceId, and ReportId from the same event so the originating event and affected device can be identified. Timestamp is already present, so DeviceId and ReportId must also be projected.

**Learn more:** [Create custom detection rules in Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/custom-detection-rules)

questions.question:
You need to visualize Microsoft Sentinel data and enrich it by using third-party data sources to identify indicators of compromise (IoC).  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel notebooks provide programmable data analysis and visualization. They can use MSTICPy and other Python libraries to retrieve and enrich investigation data from third-party sources, including data used to identify indicators of compromise (IoCs).\
\
**Learn more:** [Jupyter notebooks with Microsoft Sentinel hunting capabilities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/notebooks) · [What is Microsoft Sentinel SIEM?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/overview)

questions.question:
You need to visualize Microsoft Sentinel data and enrich it by using third-party data sources to identify indicators of compromise (IoC).  
  
What should you use?

options.text: a Conditional Access policy in Microsoft Entra

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID Protection detects high user risk that indicates a potentially compromised account. High user risk is a Continuous Access Evaluation critical event; Exchange Online can use it to invalidate existing Outlook on the web access and require reauthentication in near real time.

**Learn more:** [Continuous access evaluation in Microsoft Entra](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-continuous-access-evaluation) · [Protecting tokens in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/protecting-tokens-microsoft-entra-id)

User1 has been assigned the Copilot Contributor role.  
  
During an investigation, User1 submits a prompt and receives a notification that Copilot for Security cannot respond to requests because security compute unit (SCU) usage is approaching the provisioned-capacity limit.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can use Copilot for Security to produce a successful response.  
  
What should User1 do?

options.text: Wait one hour and resubmit the prompt.
Run the Microsoft Sentinel Optimization Workbook.
Open a second Copilot for Security session and submit the prompt.

questions.explanation:
When available provisioned and overage SCU capacity has been consumed, Copilot for Security stops accepting prompts until capacity refreshes in the next hourly block. Changing provisioned SCUs requires an Azure capacity owner or contributor, not the Copilot Contributor role. Therefore, waiting one hour and submitting the prompt again allows capacity to become available.

**Learn more:** [Manage security compute unit usage in Security Copilot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/security/manage-usage)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are configuring Azure Sentinel.  
  
You need to send a Microsoft Teams message to a channel whenever a sign-in from a suspicious IP address is detected.  
  
Which two actions should you take in Azure Sentinel? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Associate a playbook to an incident.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel playbooks automate response actions and can send notifications to a Microsoft Teams channel. Associating the playbook with an incident enables it to run when the relevant incident is created. [Automate threat response with playbooks in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/automate-responses-with-playbooks)

**Learn more:** [Automate threat response with playbooks in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/automate-responses-with-playbooks) · [Use a Microsoft Sentinel playbook to stop potentially compromised users](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/tutorial-respond-threats-playbook)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
You need to configure Defender for Cloud to mitigate these risks:  
  
- Vulnerabilities in application source code  
- Exploitation toolkits in declarative templates  
- Operations originating from malicious IP addresses  
- Exposed secrets  
  
Which two Defender for Cloud services should you use? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
> NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for DevOps scans connected development environments and repositories for code vulnerabilities, infrastructure-as-code issues, and exposed secrets. Microsoft Defender for Resource Manager monitors Azure resource-management operations and detects suspicious activity, including operations from malicious IP addresses and use of exploitation toolkits.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender for Resource Manager - Benefits and Features](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-resource-manager-introduction) · [Configure agentless code scanning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/agentless-code-scanning)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription containing 100 Windows 10 devices.  
  
You onboard the devices to Microsoft Defender 365.  
  
You need to ensure that remote shell connections to the onboarded devices can be initiated from the Microsoft 365 Defender portal.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Modify the permissions for Microsoft 365 Defender.
From Advanced features in the Endpoints settings of the Microsoft 365 Defender portal, enable automated investigation.

questions.explanation:
Live response supplies a remote shell connection to onboarded devices. Initiating a live-response session requires the appropriate RBAC role permissions, and device groups are subsequently assigned to roles to scope access to devices. Therefore, configure RBAC before creating device groups or assigning live-response capabilities.

**Learn more:** [Investigate entities on devices using live response in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/live-response) · [Create and manage roles for role-based access control](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/user-roles)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 and contains 1,000 Windows devices.  
  
You have a PowerShell script named Script1.ps1 that is signed digitally.  
  
You need to ensure that you can run Script1.ps1 in a live response session on one of the devices.  
  
What should you do first from the live response session?

options.text: Modify the PowerShell execution policy of the device.

questions.explanation: Scripts must be **uploaded to the library** before they can be executed in a Defender for Endpoint live response session. This is a prerequisite step that makes the script available in the live response environment. Only after uploading can you reference and run the script within an active live response session.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 and contains 1,000 Windows devices.  
  
You have a PowerShell script named Script1.ps1 that is signed digitally.  
  
You need to ensure that you can run Script1.ps1 in a live response session on one of the devices.  
  
What should you do first from the live response session?

options.text: Add a parameter and modify the trigger.
Add a custom data connector and modify the trigger.
Add a condition and modify the action.
Add an alert and modify the action.

questions.explanation:
A Sentinel playbook's trigger schema is fixed by the incident/alert data it receives, so it cannot be extended with an arbitrary owner parameter. Instead, you add a condition step to the workflow that resolves the resource's owner (for example, by looking up the resource or its tags) and then modify the Send Email action's recipient field to use that dynamic value in place of the hard-coded distribution group.

**Learn more:** [Supported triggers and actions in Microsoft Sentinel playbooks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/playbook-triggers-actions)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft 365 Defender.  
  
You need to identify every entity affected by an incident.  
  
Which tab should you use in the Microsoft 365 Defender portal?
questions.explanation:
The **Evidence and Response** tab displays the supported events and suspicious entities associated with alerts in an incident, including affected entities such as devices, files, users, cloud apps, and mailboxes.\
\
**Learn more:** [Investigate incidents in the Microsoft Defender portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/investigate-incidents)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.  
  
You are investigating an incident that involves multiple alerts, events, and entities.  
  
You need to create a bookmark for the investigation. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
Which settings should you use?
questions.explanation:
Bookmarks are created by running a query and selecting results to save. Microsoft documents this exact scenario, adding bookmarks for an incident under investigation, as a Hunting-blade workflow: run a hunting query, select the relevant events or entities, and choose \"Add bookmark\" to attach them to the incident with minimal setup.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use bookmarks in hunting investigations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/bookmarks)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
You discover that when Microsoft Defender for Endpoint generates alerts for a commonly used executable file, it causes alert fatigue.  
  
You need to tune the alerts.  
  
Which two actions can an alert tuning rule perform for the alerts? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation: Alert tuning rules can perform two actions to reduce alert fatigue: hide (removes alerts from the incident queue while preserving them in logs) and resolve (marks alerts as resolved, indicating no further action required). Tuning rules cannot delete alerts permanently, merge multiple alerts, or assign them to specific users. These two actions provide effective noise reduction while maintaining audit trails.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
You discover that when Microsoft Defender for Endpoint generates alerts for a commonly used executable file, it causes alert fatigue.  
  
You need to tune the alerts.  
  
Which two actions can an alert tuning rule perform for the alerts? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A custom detection rule's built-in lookback window is tied to its run frequency (24h -> 30-day lookback, 12h -> 48h, 3h -> 12h, 1h -> 4h). Only the 24-hour frequency provides a lookback long enough to capture the full 14-day communication history needed to spot a device beaconing once every 50 hours, making it the only option that satisfies the 14-day requirement while still running as often as possible.

**Learn more:** [Custom detection rules in Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/custom-detection-rules)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to limit cloud apps running on CLIENT1 to satisfy the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint requirements.  
  
Which two configurations should be modified? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: the Onboarding settings from Device management in Microsoft Defender Security Center
Cloud App Security anomaly detection policies
Advanced features from Settings in Microsoft Defender Security Center
the Cloud Discovery settings in Cloud App Security

questions.explanation:
Cloud-app access enforcement requires enabling Custom network indicators in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and enabling Enforce app access in the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integration under Cloud Discovery. These settings allow apps marked as unsanctioned to be synchronized and blocked through network protection.

**Learn more:** [Govern discovered apps using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/mde-govern)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
You have an Amazon Web Services (AWS) subscription that contains multiple virtual machines running Windows Server.  
  
You need to enable Microsoft Defender for Servers on the virtual machines.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
> NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.

options.text: From Defender for Cloud, enable agentless scanning.
Onboard the virtual machines to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
From Defender for Cloud, configure the AWS connector.
Install the Azure Virtual Machine Agent (VM Agent) on each virtual machine.
From Defender for Cloud, configure auto-provisioning.

questions.explanation:
Defender for Cloud must connect the AWS account by using the AWS connector so it can discover and manage the AWS workload. Defender for Servers protection on non-Azure servers uses the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint sensor, so the Windows Server virtual machines must be onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.

**Learn more:** [Connect your AWS account - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/quickstart-onboard-aws) · [Connect your non-Azure servers to Microsoft Defender for Cloud with Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/onboard-machines-with-defender-for-endpoint)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a device named Device1.  
  
In the Microsoft Defender portal, you find that an alert was triggered for Device1.  
  
From the Device inventory page, you isolate Device1.  
  
You need to obtain a list of programs installed on Device1.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Initiate a live response session and run the processes command.
Initiate an automated investigation and view the results in the Action center.
Initiate a live response session and run the analyze command.
Run an advanced hunting query against the DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory table.

questions.explanation:
The `DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory` advanced-hunting table contains Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management inventory records for software currently installed on devices. Filtering that table for Device1 returns its installed-program list. The `processes` live-response command reports running processes, while `analyze` assesses a specified entity.

**Learn more:** [DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory table in the advanced hunting schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-devicetvmsoftwareinventory-table) · [Investigate entities on devices using live response in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/live-response)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named SW1.  
  
You need to identify which anomaly rules are enabled in SW1.  
  
What should you review in Microsoft Sentinel?
questions.explanation: In Microsoft Sentinel, anomaly rules and their enablement status are reviewed in the Analytics section, specifically under the Anomalies tab. This tab displays all available anomaly rules in a grid view and indicates which rules are currently enabled or disabled. Content hub manages rule deployment, entity behavior provides insights on user/entity actions, and Settings handles workspace configuration.

options.text: Change Discovery mode to Standard discovery.
Set Enable EDR in block mode to On.

questions.explanation:
Automatic attack disruption requires Microsoft Defender for Endpoint device discovery to be set to Standard discovery for automatic initiation of the Contain Device action. A Microsoft 365 E5 subscription meets the licensing requirement.

**Learn more:** [Configure automatic attack disruption in Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/configure-attack-disruption)

A security administrator receives email notifications from Azure Defender for activities such as possible malware being uploaded to a storage account and possible successful brute-force attacks.  
  
The security administrator does **not** receive email notifications for activities such as failed antimalware actions and suspicious network activity, although the alerts appear in Azure Security Center.  
  
You need to ensure that the security administrator receives email notifications for all activities.  
  
What should you configure in the Security Center settings?

options.text: the severity level of email notifications
the integration settings for Threat detection

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud email notifications can be configured with a minimum alert severity. Setting the notification severity level low enough causes notifications to be sent for lower-severity alerts as well as higher-severity alerts.

**Learn more:** [Configure email notifications for alerts and attack paths](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/configure-email-notifications)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to stream Microsoft Graph activity logs to a third-party security information and event management (SIEM) tool. The solution must require minimal administrative effort.  
  
Where should you stream the logs?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Graph activity logs can be streamed through an Azure Event Hubs namespace to third-party SIEM solutions. Event Hubs provides the supported real-time integration path, avoiding the additional collection or export processes that would be needed with storage or a Log Analytics workspace.

**Learn more:** [Access Microsoft Graph activity logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/microsoft-graph-activity-logs-overview) · [Access activity logs in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-access-activity-logs)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace with Microsoft Sentinel data lake enabled for long-term retention.  
  
You have a Microsoft Security Operations Center (SOC) that uses Jupyter notebooks for advanced investigations.  
  
You run a weekly, hypothesis-driven hunting query to identify potential lateral movement. The query searches for multiple failed sign-ins followed by a successful sign-in.  
  
You need to offload the query's heavy computation and persist the processed results in the data lake.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use livestream to continuously append the results of a second hunting query.
Every hour, create a watchlist from raw events.

questions.explanation:
A scheduled notebook job executes Jupyter notebook processing against Microsoft Sentinel data lake data on a recurring schedule. It is designed for heavier notebook-based computation and can write processed output to custom tables in the data lake or analytics tier, making it suitable for recurring threat-hunting and investigation workflows.

**Learn more:** [Running notebooks on the Microsoft Sentinel data lake](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/datalake/notebooks) · [Manage KQL jobs in the Microsoft Sentinel data lake](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/datalake/kql-manage-jobs)

You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named Workspace1 and a firewall named FW1. FW1 logs are ingested into Workspace1. Firewall events are usually ingested about two minutes after they occur, and occasionally as late as five minutes afterward.  
  
A scheduled analytics rule runs every five minutes and queries the `TimeGenerated` value for the preceding five minutes.  
  
You need to minimize missed detections resulting from ingestion delays and avoid duplicate alerts between rule runs.  
  
How should you modify the analytics rule query?

options.text: Increase the rule frequency to one minute and keep the lookback window on TimeGenerated at five minutes.
Keep the lookback window on TimeGenerated at five minutes and add | where ingestion_time() > ago(5m).
Increase the lookback window on TimeGenerated to 10 minutes and add | where ingestion_time() > ago(5m).
Increase the lookback window on TimeGenerated to 10 minutes and do NOT add ingestion_time() filter.

questions.explanation:
To cover events that arrive up to five minutes after their `TimeGenerated` timestamp, the `TimeGenerated` lookback must span the five-minute rule interval plus the maximum five-minute ingestion delay, for a total of 10 minutes. Because this creates overlapping time ranges across executions, `ingestion_time() > ago(5m)` restricts each execution to records ingested during its own five-minute interval, preventing duplicates.

**Learn more:** [Handle ingestion delay in scheduled analytics rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/ingestion-delay)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft 365 Defender.  
  
You plan to create a hunting query in Microsoft Defender.  
  
You need to create a custom tracked query that will be used to evaluate the subscription's threat status.  
  
From which page in the Microsoft 365 Defender portal should you create the query?
questions.explanation:
Custom tracked queries are created in Threat Explorer by saving a query and selecting **Track this query**. The query then runs automatically, and its results appear in Threat tracker. [Threat trackers in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/threat-trackers)\
\
**Learn more:** [Threat trackers in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/threat-trackers)

questions.question:
Solution: You configure Controlled folder access.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation: Configuring Controlled Folder Access does not meet the goal. Controlled Folder Access (a Microsoft Defender Antivirus feature) only operates when Defender Antivirus is in active mode. When a third-party antivirus is installed, Defender reverts to passive mode and Controlled Folder Access is disabled. EDR in block mode would provide the necessary protection, as it functions independently of Antivirus mode.

questions.question:
Solution: You enable automated investigation and response (AIR).  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation: Enabling Automated Investigation and Response (AIR) does not meet the goal in this scenario. AIR's remediation capabilities depend on Microsoft Defender Antivirus being in active mode or running in EDR in block mode. When Defender Antivirus is in passive mode (due to third-party antivirus presence), AIR cannot execute remediation actions. EDR in block mode or enabling Defender in active mode would be required.

questions.question:
Solution: You enable endpoint detection and response (EDR) in block mode.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
EDR in block mode provides post-breach protection on devices where Microsoft Defender Antivirus is in passive mode alongside a third-party antivirus solution. It can block and remediate malicious artifacts detected by EDR that the primary antivirus product missed.\
\
**Learn more:** [Endpoint detection and response in block mode - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode)

questions.question:
Solution: You enable Live Response.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Live Response is an interactive remote shell for investigation and response actions. EDR in block mode is the feature that supplies post-breach protection by detecting and remediating malicious artifacts missed by a non-Microsoft antivirus product while Microsoft Defender Antivirus runs in passive mode.\
\
**Learn more:** [Endpoint detection and response in block mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/edr-in-block-mode) · [Investigate entities on devices using live response in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/defender-endpoint/live-response)

questions.question:
Solution: From **Security alerts**, select the alert, choose **Take Action**, and then expand the **Mitigate the threat** section.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The **Mitigate the threat** section of a security alert’s **Take action** tab provides the manual remediation steps for that alert. These recommended actions support resolving the detected threat.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage and respond to security alerts - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/manage-respond-alerts)

questions.question:
Solution: Download the report from **Regulatory compliance**.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
A Regulatory compliance report is intended to report compliance posture against standards. To view guidance related to a security alert, use the security alert details, which include mitigation steps and recommendations to help prevent future attacks.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage and respond to security alerts - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/manage-respond-alerts) · [Assign regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/assign-regulatory-compliance-standards)

questions.question:
Solution: In **Security alerts**, select the alert, choose **Take action**, and expand the **Prevent future attacks** section.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
The **Prevent future attacks** section in an alert’s **Take action** tab provides security recommendations that help reduce the attack surface, improve security posture, and prevent future attacks.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage and respond to security alerts - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/manage-respond-alerts)

questions.question:
Your organization uses Azure Sentinel.  
  
A newly hired security analyst says she cannot assign or resolve incidents in Azure Sentinel.  
  
You need to ensure that the analyst is able to assign and resolve incidents. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to the analyst?
questions.explanation:
The Azure Sentinel Responder role includes the ability to manage incidents, which covers assigning and resolving them, without granting the broader resource-management permissions provided by Azure Sentinel Contributor. Azure Sentinel Reader is view-only, and Logic App Contributor applies to Logic Apps and playbooks rather than incident management.\
\
**Learn more:** [Roles and permissions in the Microsoft Sentinel platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/roles)

options.text: From the workspace created by Defender for Cloud, set the data collection level to Common.
From the Microsoft Endpoint Manager admin center, enable automatic enrollment.
From the Azure portal, create an Azure Event Grid subscription.
From the workspace created by Defender for Cloud, set the data collection level to All Events.
From Defender for Cloud in the Azure portal, enable automatic provisioning for the virtual machines.

questions.explanation:
In the legacy Defender for Cloud agent-based configuration, automatic provisioning deploys the required monitoring agent to the virtual machines at subscription scale. Setting the Defender for Cloud-created Log Analytics workspace to the Common collection level gathers the standard security events while avoiding the additional ingestion volume and cost of collecting All Events. This legacy Log Analytics agent auto-provisioning capability has since been retired for new configurations.

**Learn more:** [Overview of the extensions that collect data from workloads](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/monitoring-components) · [Prepare for retirement of the Log Analytics agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/adaptive-application-controls)
