lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your Azure subscription uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
You need to configure Defender for Cloud to mitigate these risks:  
  
- Vulnerabilities in the application source code  
- Exploitation toolkits in declarative templates  
- Operations originating from malicious IP addresses  
- Exposed secrets  
  
Which two Defender for Cloud services should you use? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct answer is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for DevOps identifies code vulnerabilities and exposed secrets in repositories and CI/CD environments. Microsoft Defender for Resource Manager monitors Azure resource-management operations and detects activity from malicious IP addresses and exploitation toolkits, including MicroBurst and PowerZure.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender for Resource Manager - Benefits and Features](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-resource-manager-introduction) · [Microsoft Defender for Cloud DevOps Security Benefits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-devops-introduction)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have five on-premises Linux servers.  
  
You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
You need to use Defender for Cloud to protect the Linux servers. What should you install on the servers first?
questions.explanation:
The Azure Connected Machine agent onboards an on-premises server as an Azure Arc-enabled server, connecting it to the Azure subscription so Defender for Cloud can protect it and deploy required extensions. The other agents or extensions do not establish that initial Azure Arc connection.

**Learn more:** [Connect your non-Azure machines to Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/azure/defender-for-cloud/quickstart-onboard-machines) · [Determine data residency requirements for multicloud security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/plan-multicloud-security-determine-data-residency-requirements)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to ensure that Microsoft Defender XDR generates an alert when attackers try to connect to a specific device. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do in the Microsoft Defender portal?

options.text: Create a deception rule that includes a decoy.
Tag an existing device as a honeytoken entity.
Create a deception rule that includes a lure.
Tag an existing device as a sensitive entity.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Identity supports tagging devices as honeytokens. Honeytoken entities are traps for malicious actors, and authentication activity involving a honeytoken generates an alert. Tagging the existing device therefore provides the required alerting with minimal configuration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Entity tags in Microsoft Defender for Identity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-for-identity/entity-tags)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a virtual machine named VM1 that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
Microsoft Defender for Cloud is configured for automatic provisioning with Azure Monitor Agent.  
  
You need to create a custom alert-suppression rule to suppress false-positive alerts for suspicious PowerShell usage on VM1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From Microsoft Defender for Cloud, export the alerts to a Log Analytics workspace.
From Microsoft Defender for Cloud, add a workflow automation.
On VM1, trigger a PowerShell alert.
On VM1, run the Get-MPThreatCatalog cmdlet.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud suppression rules cannot suppress an alert type that has not previously been triggered in the relevant subscription or management group. Generating a suspicious PowerShell alert on VM1 establishes the alert type and supplies the alert context required to create a rule that targets it.

**Learn more:** [Suppress alerts from Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/alerts-suppression-rules)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Sentinel.  
  
You need to create a custom report that visualizes sign-in information over time.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel workbooks provide custom interactive reports and visualizations based on log queries, including charts that show Microsoft Entra sign-in activity over time.\
\
**Learn more:** [Visualize and monitor your data by using workbooks in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/azure/sentinel/monitor-your-data)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You use Azure Sentinel.  
  
You need to receive a near-real-time alert whenever Azure Storage account keys are enumerated.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
The Azure Activity data connector ingests subscription-level Azure Resource Manager operations, including management operations such as enumerating Storage account keys. An analytics rule evaluates the ingested activity and generates an alert when its detection criteria are met.

**Learn more:** [Find your Microsoft Sentinel data connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/data-connectors-reference) · [Create scheduled analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-analytics-rules)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a custom analytics rule that detects threats in Azure Sentinel. You find that the analytics rule has stopped running. The rule was disabled, and its name is prefixed with **AUTO DISABLED**.  
  
What could have caused this issue?

options.text: There are connectivity issues between the data sources and Log Analytics.
The number of alerts exceeded 10,000 within two minutes.
The rule query takes too long to run and times out.
Permissions to one of the data sources of the rule query were modified.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel automatically disables a scheduled analytics rule and prefixes its name with "AUTO DISABLED" after consecutive permanent failures. A change to permissions for a data source used by the rule query is a permanent failure because the query can no longer access that resource without intervention.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshooting analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/troubleshoot-analytics-rules)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a Microsoft SharePoint Online site named Site1.  
  
You need to enable Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session control for Site1.  
  
Which policy type should you create first?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session controls depend on a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy configured for Conditional Access App Control. That policy routes SharePoint Online traffic through Defender for Cloud Apps, enabling the later session policy to monitor or control the session.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use Defender for Cloud Apps Conditional Access app control](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/conditional-access-app-control-how-to-overview) · [Create Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/session-policy-aad)

You have an Azure subscription with Microsoft Defender for Cloud enabled.  
  
A virtual machine named Server1 runs Windows Server 2022 and is hosted in Amazon Web Services (AWS).  
  
You need to collect logs and remediate vulnerabilities for Server1 by using Defender for Cloud.  
  
What should you install on Server1 first?
questions.explanation:
An AWS EC2 instance must have Azure Arc for servers installed before Defender for Cloud can use Arc-connected-machine extensions such as Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and a vulnerability-assessment solution. The Azure Connected Machine agent onboards the Windows Server 2022 machine to Azure Arc; Windows Server 2022 is supported by that agent.

**Learn more:** [Connect your AWS Account - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/quickstart-onboard-aws) · [Connected Machine agent prerequisites - Azure Arc](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-arc/servers/prerequisites)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises network.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Identity.  
  
From the Microsoft Defender portal, you investigate an incident on a device named Device1 of a user named User1. The incident contains the following Defender for Identity alert.  
  
Suspected identity theft (pass-the-ticket) (external ID 2018)  
  
You need to contain the incident without affecting users and devices. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Reset the password for all the accounts that previously signed in to Device1.
Disable User1, quarantine Device1, and reset the password for all the accounts that previously signed in to Device1.

questions.explanation: A pass-the-ticket attack reuses an already-issued Kerberos ticket, so neither disabling User1's account nor resetting any account's password invalidates a ticket that is still within its lifetime — the stolen ticket keeps working regardless of those changes. Quarantining Device1 cuts the compromised endpoint off from the network, immediately stopping further use of the stolen ticket from that device, while leaving User1's account enabled and every other account and device untouched.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company deploys the following services:  
  
- Microsoft Defender for Identity  
- Microsoft Defender for Endpoint  
- Microsoft Defender for Office 365  
  
You need to give a security analyst the ability to use the Microsoft 365 security center. The analyst must be able to approve and reject pending actions created by Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which two roles should you assign to the analyst? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: the Compliance Data Administrator in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)
the Active remediation actions role in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
the Security Administrator role in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)
the Security Reader role in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)

questions.explanation:
The Active remediation actions role in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint authorizes a user to take response actions, including approving or dismissing pending remediation actions. The Azure AD Security Reader role provides security-center access without the broader administrative privileges of the Security Administrator role, satisfying least privilege.

**Learn more:** [Go to the Action center to view and approve automated investigation and remediation tasks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/m365d-action-center) · [Create and manage roles for role-based access control in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/user-roles)

questions.question:
You need to correlate data in the **SecurityEvent** Log Analytics table to satisfy the Microsoft Sentinel requirements for using UEBA.  
  
Which Log Analytics table should you use?
questions.explanation:
The **IdentityInfo** table contains UEBA-synchronized identity details, including on-premises account SIDs, user metadata, group memberships, and roles. It can be joined to **SecurityEvent** data using the security-event user SID and `IdentityInfo.AccountSID` to enrich security events for UEBA analysis.\
\
**Learn more:** [Investigate incidents with UEBA data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/investigate-with-ueba) · [Microsoft Sentinel UEBA reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/ueba-reference)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to deploy the native cloud connector to Account 1 to meet the Microsoft Defender for Cloud requirements.  
  
What should you do first in Account1?

options.text: Create an AWS user for Defender for Cloud.
Deploy the AWS Systems Manager (SSM) agent.
Create an Access control (IAM) role for Defender for Cloud.

questions.explanation:
Azure Arc autoprovisioning for AWS EC2 instances through the Microsoft Defender for Cloud native connector requires the AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Agent. If that agent is absent, the connector cannot automate deployment of the Azure Connected Machine agent. The onboarding CloudFormation template creates the required AWS IAM authentication components.

**Learn more:** [Connect AWS accounts to Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/quickstart-onboard-aws) · [Authentication architecture for AWS connectors](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/concept-authentication-architecture-aws)

questions.question:
You need to fulfill the Microsoft Sentinel requirements for App1.  
  
What should you configure for App1?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel automation rules run Logic Apps playbooks. A playbook must use a Microsoft Sentinel connector trigger—such as an incident, alert, or entity trigger—which defines the input schema that Sentinel sends when it invokes the workflow. Configuring that trigger makes the Logic App available for use by automation rules.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Logic Apps for Microsoft Sentinel playbooks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/logic-apps-playbooks)

questions.question:
You need to ensure that hunting queries can be run to satisfy the Microsoft Sentinel requirements.  
  
Which type of workspace should you create?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel Jupyter notebooks are used for advanced hunting and investigation, and running them from Microsoft Sentinel requires access to an Azure Machine Learning workspace. That workspace provides the notebook execution environment for the hunting queries.\
\
**Learn more:** [Jupyter notebooks with Microsoft Sentinel hunting capabilities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/notebooks)

questions.question:
You need to identify the mean time metrics required to meet the Microsoft Sentinel requirements.  
  
Which workbook should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Sentinel **Security Operations Efficiency** workbook provides SOC incident-performance metrics, including mean time to triage and mean time to closure. These metrics measure the required incident triage and closing times.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage your SOC better with incident metrics in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/manage-soc-with-incident-metrics)

questions.question:
You need to minimize the effort needed to investigate false-positive alerts from Microsoft Defender for Identity.  
  
What should you review?

options.text: the resolution method of the source computer
the certainty of the source computer

questions.explanation:
Defender for Identity includes the certainty of computer name resolution in alert evidence. When the source computer has low resolution certainty, verify the actual device that used the IP address; a Suspected DCSync attack alert is a false positive when the activity originated from a domain controller. This certainty value focuses investigation on whether the reported source device is reliable.\
\
**Learn more:** [Network Name Resolution - Microsoft Defender for Identity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-for-identity/nnr-policy)

questions.question:
You need to implement the Defender for Cloud requirements.  
  
What should you configure for Server2?

options.text: the Azure Automanage machine configuration extension for Windows

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud excludes individual machines from agentless scanning by using environment tags. Assigning Server2 an Azure resource tag and configuring that tag and value as an agentless-scanning exclusion lets Defender for Servers Plan 2 remain enabled while Server2 is skipped during scanning.\
\
**Learn more:** [Exclude machines from agentless scanning - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/exclude-machines-agentless-scanning)

questions.question:
You need to implement the Defender for Cloud requirements.  
  
Which subscription-level role should be assigned to Group1?
questions.explanation:
The Security Admin role can enable or disable Microsoft Defender plans and add or assign initiatives, including regulatory compliance standards. It provides the required Defender for Cloud and policy-management permissions without the broader full-resource access granted by Owner.\
\
**Learn more:** [User roles and permissions in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/permissions) · [Azure built-in roles for Security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/security)

questions.question:
You need to ensure that the HuntingQuery1 configuration fulfills the Microsoft Sentinel requirements.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel automatically runs hunting queries that are saved to favorites each time the Hunting page is accessed. Therefore, saving HuntingQuery1 as a favorite satisfies the automatic-execution requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Hunting capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/hunting)

questions.question:
You need to implement the scheduled rule for generating incidents based on rulequery1.  
  
What should you configure first?
questions.explanation:
To group recurring alerts from the same Azure Cloud Shell user into one incident, the rule needs an Account entity mapped from the query output. Microsoft Sentinel alert grouping can group alerts when selected mapped entities match, so entity mapping must be configured before grouping by the user entity. The query’s `Account_0_Name` and `Account_0_UPNSuffix` fields provide the account values for that mapping.\
\
**Learn more:** [Scheduled analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/scheduled-rules-overview) · [Map data fields to Microsoft Sentinel entities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/map-data-fields-to-entities)

questions.question:
You need to implement the scheduled rule for generating incidents based on rulequery1.  
  
What should you configure first?

options.text: a playbook with an incident trigger
a playbook with an alert trigger
a playbook with an entity trigger

questions.explanation:
To conditionally close an incident, Microsoft Sentinel uses an automation rule to invoke a playbook that updates the incident. Automation rules based on an incident trigger can run only playbooks that start with the Microsoft Sentinel incident trigger, so that playbook must exist before it can be selected in the automation rule. [Create and use Microsoft Sentinel automation rules to manage response](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-manage-use-automation-rules)

**Learn more:** [Create and use Microsoft Sentinel automation rules to manage response](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-manage-use-automation-rules) · [Create and manage Microsoft Sentinel playbooks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/create-playbooks)

questions.question:
You need to set up event monitoring for Server1. The solution must satisfy the Microsoft Sentinel requirements.  
  
What should you create first?

options.text: a Microsoft Sentinel scheduled query rule

questions.explanation:
The Windows Security Events via AMA connector uses a Data Collection Rule (DCR) to define which Windows Security events the Azure Monitor agent collects and to associate the rule with Server1. Data must be collected through that DCR before analytics or automation can process it.\
\
**Learn more:** [Connect Microsoft Sentinel to other Microsoft services with a Windows agent-based data connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/connect-services-windows-based)

questions.question:
You need to ensure that the members of Group1 can fulfill the Microsoft Sentinel requirements.  
  
Which role should be assigned to Group1?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel playbooks are implemented as Azure Logic Apps workflows. The **Logic App Contributor** role permits users to create, edit, and manage logic apps and therefore provides the required ability to create and edit playbooks. The other listed roles support running playbooks or automation behavior rather than playbook authoring.\
\
**Learn more:** [Roles and permissions in the Microsoft Sentinel platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/roles) · [Create and manage Microsoft Sentinel playbooks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/create-playbooks)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace connected to the Microsoft Sentinel data lake.  
  
In Microsoft Visual Studio Code, you plan to run Jupyter notebooks using a GitHub Copilot agent that hunts for threats. The agent will use natural-language queries to find relevant tables and query long-term data in the data lake.  
  
You need to connect the GitHub Copilot agent to the Microsoft Sentinel Model Context Protocol (MCP) collection endpoint.  
  
Which URL should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Sentinel Data exploration MCP collection supports natural-language discovery of relevant data lake tables and retrieval/querying of Microsoft Sentinel data lake data. Its endpoint is `https://sentinel.microsoft.com/mcp/data-exploration`.

**Learn more:** [Explore Microsoft Sentinel data lake with data exploration collection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/datalake/sentinel-mcp-data-exploration-tool)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace that contains a custom workbook named Workbook1.  
  
You need to create a visual based on the SecurityEvent table. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
• Identify the number of security events ingested during the past week.  

• Display the count of events by day in a timechart.  
  
What should you add to Workbook1?
questions.explanation: A **query** retrieves and aggregates data from the SecurityEvent table. You can write a KQL query to count events from the past week and group by day, then render the results as a timechart visualization. Metrics are predefined calculations, query groups are organizational, and links/tabs provide navigation—none directly visualize query results.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 and contains 500 Windows devices.  
  
You plan to create a Microsoft Defender XDR custom deception rule.  
  
You need to ensure that the rule will be applied to only 10 specific devices.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Add custom lures to the rule.
Add the IP address of each device to the list of decoy accounts and hosts of the rule.
Add the devices to a group.
Assign a tag to the devices.

questions.explanation: To scope a deception rule to specific devices, you must first assign a tag to the 10 target devices. The deception rule configuration then allows you to select 'Devices with specific tags' in its scope section, restricting the rule to devices bearing that tag. Adding devices to a group or modifying lure content does not enable device-level scoping for deception rules.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 and contains 500 Windows devices.  
  
You plan to create a Microsoft Defender XDR custom deception rule.  
  
You need to ensure that the rule will be applied to only 10 specific devices.  
  
What should you do first?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint configures automated investigation and remediation through device groups. A device group can identify the 50 pilot devices and assign the **Full – remediate threats automatically** automation level, isolating the pilot from the remaining devices while requiring only one scoped configuration.

**Learn more:** [Configure automated investigation and remediation capabilities in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/configure-automated-investigations-remediation) · [Automation levels in automated investigation and remediation capabilities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/automation-levels)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
You are investigating an attacker that is known to use the Microsoft Graph API as an attack vector. The attacker performs the tactics shown the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783739287866-q72dtxbq.png)  
  
You need to search for malicious activities in your organization.  
  
Which tactics can you analyze by using the MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs table?
questions.explanation: All three tactics—Conditional Access policy reconnaissance, mailbox reconnaissance, and guest user invitations—utilize Microsoft Graph API calls and are thus logged in the MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs table. These reconnaissance and privilege-escalation activities would be captured when performed through Graph API endpoints (e.g., /me/mailboxSettings, /chats, /invitations).

questions.question:
Solution: From Defender, you modify the search criteria of the audit search to reduce the number of returned records, and then you export the results. From Excel, you perform the Get & Transform Data operations by using the new export.  
  
Does this meet the requirement?
questions.explanation: The solution meets the requirement. Excel's Get & Transform Data feature evaluates JSON properties from the first 1,000 rows of exported audit data. If additional JSON properties exist in records beyond row 1,000, those properties and their columns will not be created during transformation. Reducing the audit search criteria ensures fewer total records and prevents property omission, allowing Excel to successfully transform all relevant JSON fields into columns.

questions.question:
Solution: From Excel, you apply filters to the existing columns in File1.csv to reduce the number of rows, and then you perform the Get & Transform Data operations to parse the AuditData column.  
  
Does this meet the requirement?
questions.explanation:
Filtering the Operations column (an existing column) to cut down the number of rows before running Get & Transform Data is exactly the workaround Microsoft documents for cases where distinct JSON properties in AuditData appear beyond the first 1,000 rows; reducing rows before the parse step lets Power Query pick up the properties needed, so this solution satisfies the requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Export, configure, and view audit log records](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-log-export-records)

questions.question:
Solution: From Defender, you modify the search criteria of the audit search to increase the number of returned records, and then you export the results. From Excel, you perform the Get & Transform Data operations by using the new export.  
  
Does this meet the requirement?
questions.explanation: The solution does not meet the requirement. Increasing the number of returned records in an audit search exacerbates the JSON property truncation problem. Excel's Get & Transform Data evaluates only the first 1,000 rows for schema inference; additional properties beyond that threshold are ignored. The correct approach is to reduce search criteria to minimize total records, ensuring all JSON properties are detected and transformed.

questions.question:
Solution: From Excel, you apply filters to the existing columns in File1.csv to reduce the number of JSON properties, and then you perform the Get 8t Transform Data operations to parse the AuditData column.  
  
Does this meet the requirement?
questions.explanation: Filtering existing columns only reduces the number of rows returned; it does nothing to make Power Query recognize or split additional JSON properties found in the AuditData column beyond the first 1,000 rows. Trimming JSON properties this way does not solve the underlying column-generation problem, so the solution does not meet the requirement.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.  
  
You are investigating an incident involving these entities:  
  
- A host named Host1  
- A user account named User1  
- An IP address of 175.45.176.99  
  
You need to update the threat intelligence list to include the entities.  
  
Which entities can you add from the Incident page?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel can add only domain names, IP addresses (IPv4 or IPv6), URLs, and file hashes as threat intelligence indicators from an incident. An IP address is supported, whereas host and user-account entities are not supported indicator types.\
\
**Learn more:** [Add entities to threat intelligence in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/add-entity-to-threat-intelligence)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.  
  
You are investigating an incident involving these entities:  
  
- A host named Host1  
- A user account named User1  
- An IP address of 175.45.176.99  
  
You need to update the threat intelligence list to include the entities.  
  
Which entities can you add from the Incident page?
questions.explanation:
The Devices node provides the Assignment Failures report, which consolidates failed assignments by device and policy. The report includes security baselines, enabling identification of both each affected device and the baseline that failed without reviewing every baseline separately.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Intune Reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/reports/overview) · [Monitor security baselines and profiles in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/security-baselines/monitor-baselines)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
You have a query that contains the following statements.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783741319516-onm2jbtw.png)  
  
You need to configure a custom detection rule that will use the query. The solution must minimize how long it takes to be notified about events that match the query.  
  
Which frequency should you select for the rule?
questions.explanation:
The KQL query unions two tables (DeviceEvents and DeviceProcessEvents), and Continuous (NRT) custom detection rules only support queries that reference a single table and a restricted set of KQL operators, excluding union, join, and functions like ingestion_time(). Because Continuous (NRT) cannot be used with this query, the fastest allowed polling interval is hourly, which minimizes notification latency among the remaining valid options.

**Learn more:** [Custom detection rules - Queries you can run continuously](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/custom-detection-rules#queries-you-can-run-continuously)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named WS1. WS1 has the Azure Activity connector and the Microsoft Entra ID connector configured.  
  
You need to investigate which accounts have the highest number of alerts and any related incident information for each alert. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first in WS1?

options.text: Use User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) to detect anomalies.
Enable User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA).
From Content hub, install the Microsoft Purview insider risk management solution.
From Content hub, install Cloud Identity Threat Protection Essentials.

questions.explanation:
User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) analyzes alerts and logs from connected data sources to create behavioral profiles for entities such as users. Its user/entity investigation experience provides alert-related entity context and supports investigation of associated incidents. Enabling UEBA in the workspace is required before those UEBA capabilities can be used; the existing Microsoft Entra ID and Azure Activity connectors provide relevant connected data sources. The Cloud Identity Threat Protection Essentials solution provides analytic rules and hunting queries, rather than this workspace-wide entity behavior capability.

**Learn more:** [Enable User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/enable-entity-behavior-analytics) · [Entity pages in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/entity-pages)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription with Microsoft 365 Defender enabled.  
  
You need to identify every change made to sensitivity labels over the previous seven days.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: the Incidents blade of the Microsoft 365 Defender portal
the Alerts settings on the Data Loss Prevention blade of the Microsoft 365 compliance center
Activity explorer in the Microsoft 365 compliance center
the Explorer settings on the Email & collaboration blade of the Microsoft 365 Defender portal

questions.question:

You need to make sure that Defender for Cloud can access the repositories in Account1.  
  
What should you do first in the Microsoft Defender for Cloud portal?

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.  
  
You need to stop a built-in Advanced Security Information Model (ASIM) parser from being updated automatically.  
  
What are two ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create a hunting query that references the built-in parser.
Build a custom unifying parser and include the built-in parser version.
Redeploy the built-in parser and specify a CallerContext parameter of Any and a SourceSpecificParser parameter of Any.
Redeploy the built-in parser and specify a CallerContext parameter of Built-in.
Create an analytics rule that includes the built-in parser.

questions.explanation:
Automatic updates can be prevented by pinning a specific version of the built-in source-specific parser in a custom unifying parser, or by excluding all built-in parsers through an exclusion record with `Any` in both the `CallerContext` and `SourceSpecificParser` fields. Query and analytics-rule references do not prevent parser updates.

**Learn more:** [Manage Advanced Security Information Model (ASIM) parsers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/normalization-manage-parsers)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
You need to add threat indicators for every IP address in the range `171.23.34.32-171.23.34.63`. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do in the Microsoft 365 Defender portal?

options.text: Create an import file that contains the individual IP addresses in the range. Select Import and import the file.
Create an import file that contains the IP address of 171.23.34.32/27. Select Import and import the file.
Select Add indicator and set the IP address to 171.23.34.32-171.23.34.63.
Select Add indicator and set the IP address to 171.23.34.32/27.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint custom IP indicators accept only individual IP addresses; IP ranges and CIDR blocks are unsupported. A CSV import can create the 32 individual IP indicators in one operation, minimizing administrative effort.

questions.question:

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to configure Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps to create alerts and initiate remediation actions when confidential files are shared externally.

You discover that, because of server-side paging, the query returns only the first page of results.

For a server-paged Microsoft Graph response, `@odata.nextLink` contains the URL for the next results page. Continue requesting the URL returned in this property until no `@odata.nextLink` is returned to retrieve the complete result set.\

You need to create a query that will display a bar graph. What should you include in the query?

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Use aggregation functions in Kusto Query Language](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/kusto/query/tutorials/use-aggregation-functions?view=microsoft-fabric)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription linked to a hybrid Azure AD tenant.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a suppression rule in Azure Security Center for 10 virtual machines used for testing. The virtual machines run Windows Server.

View the Windows event logs on the virtual machines.

questions.question:

You need to receive a notification in the Azure portal immediately when the hunting query finds a match. The solution must require minimal effort.  
  
What should you use?

A Microsoft Sentinel livestream session can be created from a hunting query and provides Azure portal notifications when new events match the query, without the overhead of maintaining a custom alert rule. Microsoft has subsequently announced the retirement of livestreams, but it is the capability that meets this scenario’s stated requirements.\
\
**Learn more:** [Detect threats by using hunting livestream in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-sg/azure/sentinel/livestream)

questions.question:
You create a hunting query in Azure Sentinel.  
  
You need to receive a notification in the Azure portal immediately when the hunting query finds a match. The solution must require minimal effort.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: Add the Security Events connector to the Azure Sentinel workspace.
Create a query that uses the workspace expression and the union operator.
Create a query that uses the resource expression and the alias operator.
Add the Azure Sentinel solution to each workspace.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel must be added to every Log Analytics workspace you want to hunt across, and a hunting query then uses the workspace() expression together with the union operator to combine the Windows event tables from each workspace—across subscriptions in the same Azure AD tenant—into a single query.

**Learn more:** [Extend Microsoft Sentinel across workspaces and tenants](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/extend-sentinel-across-workspaces-tenants)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named SW1.  
  
In SW1, you investigate an incident that is associated with the following entities:

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
Automated investigation and response (AIR) is enabled in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 and devices use full automation in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
You have an incident involving a user that received malware-infected email messages on a managed device.  
  
Which action requires manual remediation of the incident?
questions.explanation:
With AIR fully automated, Defender for Office 365 automatically soft- or hard-deletes the malicious email, and Defender for Endpoint's automated investigation can quarantine files, kill processes, and remove scheduled tasks on the managed device without human input. Isolating the device, however, is deliberately excluded from automated remediation and remains a manual response action an analyst must trigger from the device page.

**Learn more:** [Take response actions on a device](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/respond-machine-alerts)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named Workspace1 and 200 custom Advanced Security Information Model (ASIM) parsers that are based on the DNS schema.  
  
You need to make the 200 parsers available in Workspace1 while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Copy the parsers to the Azure Monitor Logs page.
Create a JSON file based on the DNS template.
Create an XML file based on the DNS template.
Create a YAML file based on the DNS template.

questions.explanation:
For a large number of ASIM parsers, use parser ARM templates instead of manually creating each Azure Monitor Logs function. The deployment workflow begins by creating a YAML file from the template for the relevant schema and parser type; the YAML is converted to an ARM template and then deployed.

**Learn more:** [Develop Microsoft Sentinel Advanced Security Information Model (ASIM) parsers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/normalization-develop-parsers)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace that contains the following tables.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783744856703-m43lbprw.png)  
  
You need to investigate the log data by using a search.  
  
Which tables can you search?
questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor search jobs can retrieve data from both analytics retention and long-term (archive) retention. Search jobs support Analytics and Basic table plans, so all four tables are searchable.\
\
**Learn more:** [Run search jobs in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/search-jobs) · [Manage data retention in a Log Analytics workspace](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/data-retention-configure)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace that contains the following tables.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783744856703-m43lbprw.png)  
  
You need to investigate the log data by using a search.  
  
Which tables can you search?
questions.explanation:
The Linux alert simulation uses a benign copy of `/bin/echo` renamed to `asc_alerttest_662jfi039n`, then runs that renamed executable with `testing eicar pipe`. The required name and arguments generate the test detection event that is reported as an Azure Defender alert.

**Learn more:** [Azure Kubernetes Service Baseline - The Hard Way, Part Deux](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/appsonazureblog/azure-kubernetes-service-baseline---the-hard-way-part-deux/4259413) · [Validate alerts in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/alert-validation)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
You enable automatic attack disruption.  
  
During a recent ransomware incident, Defender for Endpoint responded automatically to the incident.  
  
You need to review Defender for Endpoint’s automatic responses to the incident.  
  
What should you use in the Microsoft Defender portal?
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Defender portal’s unified Action center lists remediation and response actions taken automatically or manually. Automatic attack disruption actions, including Defender for Endpoint containment or remediation during ransomware incidents, can be reviewed there.

**Learn more:** [Details and results of an automatic attack disruption action - Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/autoad-results) · [Visit the Action center to see remediation actions - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/auto-investigation-action-center)

questions.question: Which rule setting should be configured to satisfy the Azure Sentinel requirements?

options.text: From Set rule logic, turn off suppression.
From Analytics rule details, configure the tactics.
From Set rule logic, map the entities.
From Analytics rule details, configure the severity.

questions.explanation:
Entity mapping is configured in **Set rule logic** and maps fields returned by an analytics-rule query to Microsoft Sentinel-recognized entities. This enriches alerts and incidents with the entities needed for investigation and response. [Create scheduled analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-analytics-rules)\
\
**Learn more:** [Create scheduled analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-analytics-rules)

questions.question:
You need to visualize Azure Sentinel data and enrich it by using third-party data sources to identify indicators of compromise (IoCs).  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel notebooks provide an interactive Jupyter environment for analysis and visualization, and MSTICPy supplies cybersecurity tools for data retrieval, analysis, enrichment, and visualization. Notebooks can also use third-party Python packages and external data sources to enrich indicators of compromise.\
\
**Learn more:** [Jupyter notebooks with Microsoft Sentinel hunting capabilities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/notebooks)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR. All client computers run Windows 11 and are onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
You have an Azure subscription containing a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.  
  
You need to ensure that an investigation package is collected whenever malware is detected on a Windows 11 computer. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: an automated alert response in Defender for Endpoint

questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint's Automated Investigation and Response (AIR) can be configured to automatically collect investigation packages when malware is detected, minimizing administrative effort compared to Sentinel automation rules or manual collection.

questions.question:
Your company uses Azure Security Center and Azure Defender.  
  
The company’s security operations team reports that it does **not** receive email notifications for security alerts. What should you configure in Security Center to enable those email notifications?
questions.explanation:
Security Center security policy contains the subscription-level email-notification configuration, including alert notification settings and recipient email addresses. Microsoft Defender for Cloud continues to provide these settings as subscription email-notification/security-contact configuration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure email notifications for alerts and attack paths - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/configure-email-notifications)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Purview.  
  
Your company has a project named Project1.  
  
You need to identify all the email messages that have the word Project1 in the subject line. The solution must search only the mailboxes of users that worked on Project1.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation: Content Search in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery enables searching email, Teams chats, and documents with flexible scoping to specific mailboxes. You can query for emails with 'Project1' in the subject line and restrict the search to mailboxes of only Project1 team members. User data search is not a standard Purview feature; audit search tracks user activities rather than email content; records management disposition handles retention policies.

questions.question:
You need to assign an RBAC role to admin1 to meet the Azure Sentinel requirements and the business requirements.  
  
Which role should be assigned?
questions.explanation: Azure Sentinel Responder grants permissions to investigate and manage Sentinel incidents, including assigning, updating, and closing them, without the broader configuration permissions provided by Azure Sentinel Contributor. Automation Operator and Automation Runbook Operator apply to Azure Automation rather than Sentinel incident response.

questions.question:
You need to assign an RBAC role to admin1 to meet the Azure Sentinel requirements and the business requirements.  
  
Which role should be assigned?

options.text: the related entities of the alert

questions.explanation:
Azure Storage Analytics logs record detailed blob service read, write, and delete requests, including `DeleteBlob` operations. These records can identify the individual blobs that were deleted.

**Learn more:** [Storage Analytics logged operations and status messages](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/storage-analytics-logged-operations-and-status-messages) · [Enable and manage Azure Storage Analytics logs (classic)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/manage-storage-analytics-logs)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Copilot for Security.  
  
You start a Copilot for Security session and enter five prompts that each provide responses.  
  
You need to create a promptbook that will use the prompts but will NOT contain the responses. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Select each prompt, and then select Create promptbook.
Create a new promptbook and include each prompt.
Enter a new prompt that has the following input: Create a promptbook from my session prompts.
Share the session, and then select Create promptbook.

questions.explanation:
Inside an active Copilot for Security session, selecting the individual prompt entries and then choosing Create promptbook packages only the selected prompts into a reusable promptbook, without carrying over the generated responses. This uses a built-in, single-step workflow and requires no re-entry of prompt text, making it the lowest-effort documented path for building a promptbook from an existing session.

**Learn more:** [Build promptbooks - Create a promptbook from an existing session](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/security/build-promptbooks#create-a-promptbook-from-an-existing-session)

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783742193388-0tl6khnf.png)  
  
You configure Microsoft Entra Internet Access.  
  
Which users can manage Microsoft Entra Internet Access?
questions.explanation:
Global Administrators can manage Microsoft Entra services, and the Global Secure Access Administrator role explicitly permits creating and managing all aspects of Microsoft Entra Internet Access. The Privileged Role Administrator role is limited to managing Microsoft Entra role assignments, Privileged Identity Management, and administrative units; it does not grant Microsoft Entra Internet Access management permissions.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)

User1 has been assigned an Azure Active Directory Premium Plan 2 license.  
  
You need to determine whether User1's identity was compromised during the previous 90 days.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
The risky users report provides user-level identity-risk information and a risk history, allowing administrators to determine whether a user's account was identified as compromised or at risk during the relevant period. Microsoft Entra ID P2 provides full access to risky-user data.

/>","className":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An Azure subscription uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud and includes 100 virtual machines running Windows Server.  
  
You need to configure Defender for Cloud to collect event data from the virtual machines. The solution must minimize administrative overhead and costs.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Configure auto-provisioning by setting the security event storage to Common.
From the Microsoft Endpoint Manager admin center, enable automatic enrollment.
From the Azure portal, create an Azure Event Grid subscription.
Configure auto-provisioning by setting the security event storage to All Events.
From Defender for Cloud in the Azure portal, enable Microsoft Defender for Servers.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Servers enables the Defender for Cloud server-protection plan. Auto-provisioning deploys the required monitoring component across server resources at scale. Collecting the Common Windows security-event set reduces data ingestion compared with collecting All Events, lowering cost while avoiding per-VM configuration effort.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription with Microsoft Defender for Cloud enabled.  
  
You have a virtual machine named Server1 that runs Windows Server 2022 and is hosted in Amazon Web Services (AWS).  
  
You need to collect logs and remediate vulnerabilities for Server1 by using Defender for Cloud.  
  
What should you install on Server1 first?
questions.explanation:
An AWS virtual machine must be onboarded as an Azure Arc-enabled server before Defender for Cloud can manage it and provide Defender for Servers capabilities. Installing the Azure Arc agent connects the machine to Azure; monitoring and vulnerability-assessment extensions can be deployed afterward. The Microsoft Monitoring Agent is retired.

You have a Microsoft 365 subscription containing a user named User1 and two Windows devices named Device1 and Device2. Device1 and Device2 are onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
The following events occur:  
  
- User1 signs in to Device1.  
- Automatic attack disruption in Microsoft Defender XDR responds to an attack on Device1 and contains User1.  
- User1 attempts to connect to Device2.  
  
Which protocols will Device2 block when User1 attempts to connect to it?
questions.explanation:
User containment in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint applies a containment policy to all onboarded devices. It blocks a contained user’s authentication-based access, file-system access, and network communication paths to limit lateral movement; the documented containment events include blocked Remote Desktop sessions, RPC resource access, and SMB file or session access. Therefore, Device2 blocks RDP, RPC, and SMB for User1.

**Learn more:** [Automatic attack disruption in Microsoft Defender](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/automatic-attack-disruption) · [DisruptionAndResponseEvents table in the advanced hunting schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-disruptionandresponseevents-table)

You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace that contains the following incident:  
  
Brute force attack against Azure Portal analytics rule has been triggered.  
  
You need to identify the geolocation information associated with the incident.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From Overview, review the Potential malicious events map.
From Incidents, review the details of the IPCustomEntity entity associated with the incident.
From Incidents, review the details of the AccountCustomEntity entity associated with the incident.
From Investigation, review insights on the incident entity.

questions.explanation: IP address entities in Sentinel incidents include geolocation data. Reviewing the **IPCustomEntity** details associated with the incident provides geolocation information such as country and region for the attacking IP addresses. This is the direct path to obtain geographic context for incident investigation.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You have the following KQL query.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783742350977-x6dobtq5.png)  
  
You need to use the query to create a Microsoft Defender XDR custom detection rule that can isolate an onboarded device.  
  
How should you change the query?

options.text: Add the AccountUpn and Timestamp columns to the project operator.
Add the DeviceId and Timestamp columns to the project operator.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender XDR applies device actions, including device isolation, to devices identified in the query results by the `DeviceId` column. Custom detections also require `Timestamp` to establish the alert event time; `ReportId` is already returned by this query. Projecting `DeviceId` and `Timestamp` makes the query suitable for a detection that can isolate the device.

**Learn more:** [Create custom detection rules in Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/custom-detection-rules)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You have the devices shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783744866238-3cjm6oa0.png)  
  
All devices are onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
You are investigating a possible malware exploit on the devices.  
  
You need to review each device's system log. The solution must minimize disruption to the devices.  
  
What should you do first for each device in the Microsoft Defender portal?
questions.explanation: Collecting an investigation package is the least disruptive action; it bundles system logs, registry data, and diagnostics into a ZIP file for offline review without isolating the device or requiring interactive monitoring.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR and contains a Windows device named Device1.  
  
The timeline of Device1 includes three files named File1.ps1, File2.exe, and File3.dll.  
  
You need to submit files for deep analysis in Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
Which files can you submit?
questions.explanation: Deep analysis in Microsoft Defender XDR supports only portable executable (PE) files—specifically .exe and .dll files. PowerShell scripts (.ps1) and other file types are not supported for deep analysis, as PE files are the primary target for executable threat analysis. File2.exe and File3.dll can be submitted, but File1.ps1 cannot.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Sentinel.  
  
You identify a new threat by using a hunting query.  
  
You need to ensure that Microsoft Sentinel detects the threat automatically. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add the query to a workbook.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules run query-based detection logic automatically and create alerts when the configured conditions are met. A hunting query can be used to create an analytics rule, making the discovered detection repeat automatically. Workbooks are for visualization, watchlists provide reference data, and playbooks automate responses to alerts rather than perform detection.

**Learn more:** [Conduct end-to-end threat hunting with Hunts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/hunts) · [Create a scheduled analytics rule from scratch](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-analytics-rules)

You have 1,000 on-premises Windows 11 Pro devices onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
You discover that an attacker performed the following actions on a device:  
  
- Modified the file system path of a registry-based antivirus exclusion  
- Downloaded a malicious file to that file system path  
  
You start a live response session on the device.  
  
You need to reverse the registry modification.  
  
Which command should you run?
questions.explanation:
In Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Live Response, the `remediate` command removes a registry entry by deleting it. Deleting the attacker-modified antivirus exclusion reverses the harmful registry change and allows the excluded path to be protected again.

**Learn more:** [Investigate entities on devices using live response in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/live-response) · [Live response command examples - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/live-response-command-examples)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have two Microsoft Entra tenants, Tenant1 and Tenant2, and each tenant is associated with an Azure subscription. Tenant1 has a group named Group1, while Tenant2 has a group named Group2.  
  
You need to deploy Microsoft Sentinel for both tenants. The solution must satisfy these requirements:  
  
- Ensure that Group1 can manage security incidents for Tenant1 and Tenant2 from a single workspace view.  
- Ensure that Group2 can manage security incidents only for Tenant2.  
- Minimize guest-account usage.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
What should the solution include?

options.text: one workspace and Privileged Identity Management (PIM)
one workspace and multiple role-based access control (RBAC) role assignments
two workspaces and granular delegated admin privileges (GDAP)

questions.explanation:
Azure Lighthouse delegates Microsoft Sentinel permissions across Microsoft Entra tenants, allowing Group1 in the managing tenant to access and manage the Sentinel workspace in Tenant2 without guest accounts. Keeping one workspace in each tenant preserves data isolation and charges associated costs to the respective tenant, while Microsoft Sentinel's multiple-workspace view enables Group1 to manage incidents across both workspaces. Group2 can receive a native Microsoft Sentinel role only in Tenant2, limiting it to that tenant.

**Learn more:** [Manage Microsoft Sentinel workspaces at scale - Azure Lighthouse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/lighthouse/how-to/manage-sentinel-workspaces) · [Extend Microsoft Sentinel across workspaces and tenants](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/extend-sentinel-across-workspaces-tenants)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
You have a custom detection rule named Rule1 that creates an alert when more than five antivirus detections are found on a device. Rule1 has a lookback period of 12 hours.  
  
You need to change the lookback period to 48 hours.  
  
What should you modify for Rule1?

options.text: the summarize operator of the KQL query
the where operator of the KQL query

questions.explanation:
In Microsoft Defender XDR custom detection rules, the lookback period is set according to the configured rule frequency. A rule that runs every three hours uses a 12-hour lookback, whereas a rule that runs every 12 hours uses a 48-hour lookback. Changing the frequency therefore changes the lookback period.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create custom detection rules in Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/custom-detection-rules)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 and contains 500 Windows devices.  
  
As part of an incident investigation, you identify the following suspected malware files:  
  
• sys  

• pdf  

• docx  

• xlsx  
  
You need to create indicator hashes to block users from downloading the files to the devices.  
  
Which files can you block by using the indicator hashes?
questions.explanation:
File hash indicators that block downloads currently apply only to portable executable (PE) content such as .exe, .dll, and .sys files. Microsoft Defender for Endpoint does not support blocking non-PE document formats like .pdf, .docx, or .xlsx through this mechanism, so only File1.sys can be blocked using an indicator hash.

**Learn more:** [Create indicators for files](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/indicator-file)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a device named Device1.  
  
In the Microsoft Defender portal, you find that an alert was triggered for Device1.  
  
From the Device inventory page, you isolate Device1.  
  
You need to obtain a list of programs installed on Device1.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Initiate a live response session and run the library command.
Run an advanced hunting query against the DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory table.
Initiate a live response session and run the analyze command.
Initiate an automated investigation and view the results in the Action center.

questions.explanation:
The `DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory` Advanced Hunting table contains the Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management inventory of software currently installed on devices. Querying and filtering it for Device1 returns its installed-program list.

**Learn more:** [DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory table in the advanced hunting schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-devicetvmsoftwareinventory-table)

questions.question:
You need to update the anomaly-detection policy settings to satisfy the Cloud App Security requirements and fix the reported issue.  
  
Which policy should you modify?
questions.explanation: The **Impossible travel** anomaly-detection policy detects activity by the same user from two geographically distant locations within an infeasible travel timeframe. Its sensitivity level can be tuned to suppress false positives from legitimate office locations. This policy specifically addresses the scenario of simultaneous connections from different geographic regions.

questions.question:
You have an Azure Sentinel workspace.  
  
You need to manually test a playbook in the Azure portal.  
  
From which location in Azure Sentinel can you run the test?
questions.explanation:
Azure Sentinel playbooks are implemented as Azure Logic Apps workflows. The Playbooks area provides access to the playbook so its workflow or trigger can be run manually for testing. Analytics is for analytic rules, Threat intelligence is for indicators, and Incidents is for incident investigation and response.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and manage Microsoft Sentinel playbooks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/create-playbooks) · [Automate and run Microsoft Sentinel playbooks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/run-playbooks)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named Workspace1.  
  
You need to exclude a built-in, source-specific Advanced Security Information Model (ASIM) parser from a built-in unified ASIM parser.  
  
What should you create in Workspace1?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel uses a watchlist to exclude built-in source-specific ASIM parsers from a built-in unified parser; built-in unified parsers cannot be edited directly for this purpose.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage Advanced Security Information Model (ASIM) parsers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/normalization-manage-parsers)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named Workspace1.  
  
You need to exclude a built-in, source-specific Advanced Security Information Model (ASIM) parser from a built-in unified ASIM parser.  
  
What should you create in Workspace1?

options.text: From Defender for Cloud, modify Microsoft Defender for Servers plan settings.
From Defender for Cloud, create a workflow automation.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Servers provides the configuration for collecting server security data and uses the connected Log Analytics workspace for eligible security-event ingestion. Its plan settings are where the server protection and related data-collection configuration is enabled; provider registration, workflow automation, and workbooks do not configure VM security-event collection.

**Learn more:** [Plan a Defender for Servers deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/plan-defender-for-servers) · [Use a Custom Data Collection Rule for Defender for Servers ingestion](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/data-collection-rule)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft SharePoint Online. You delete users from the subscription.  
  
You need to receive notifications when deleted users downloaded a large number of documents from SharePoint Online sites during the month before their accounts were deleted.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: a file policy in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
an alert policy in Microsoft Defender for Office 365

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management policy using the **Data theft by departing users** template can use a Microsoft Entra account-deleted triggering event and assess prior user activity. It detects suspicious SharePoint Online file downloads and supports cumulative activity detection over the preceding 30 days, enabling alerts for unusually numerous downloads by departing or deleted users.

**Learn more:** [Learn about Insider Risk Management policy templates](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/purview/insider-risk-management-policy-templates) · [Set policy timeframes in Insider Risk Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/insider-risk-management-settings-policy-timeframes)

options.text: And a new scheduled query rule.
Add a data connector to Azure Sentinel.
Configure a custom Threat Intelligence connector in Azure Sentinel.
Modify the trigger in the logic app.

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Sentinel playbook is an Azure Logic Apps workflow that starts from a Microsoft Sentinel incident, alert, or entity trigger. The trigger defines the input schema that Sentinel sends to the playbook; a manual trigger does not provide that integration. The logic app trigger must therefore be changed before the app can be used as a Sentinel playbook.

**Learn more:** [Azure Logic Apps for Microsoft Sentinel playbooks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/logic-apps-playbooks)

You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  

You need to assign the PCI DSS 4.0 initiative to Sub1 and have the initiative displayed in the Defender for Cloud Regulatory compliance dashboard.  
  
From Security policies in the Environment settings, you discover that the option to add more industry and regulatory standards is unavailable.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Configure the Continuous export settings for Log Analytics.
Enable the Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) plan for the subscription.
Configure the Continuous export settings for Azure Event Hubs.
Disable the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark (MCSB) assignment.

questions.explanation: To assign regulatory compliance standards like PCI DSS 4.0 to a subscription and view them in the Regulatory compliance dashboard, you must first enable the Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) plan. CSPM provides the compliance tracking and standards management capabilities; without it, the option to add industry and regulatory standards remains unavailable. Continuous export or MCSB configuration are not prerequisites.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant and a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named Workspaces1.  
  
You need to configure long-term retention for Microsoft Entra audit logs in Workspace1. The solution must maximize log retention.  
  
To what retention period should you set it?
questions.explanation:
A Log Analytics workspace can retain data for up to 12 years through total retention, which includes long-term retention. Therefore, 12 years is the maximum available retention period for the audit logs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage data retention in a Log Analytics workspace - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/data-retention-configure)

You are configuring the Security Events connector. While creating a new rule from a connector template, you choose to generate a new alert for each event. You create the following rule query.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783728832767-9hu7354x.png)  
  
By which two components can alerts be grouped into incidents? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel can group related alerts by mapped entities. `AccountCustomEntity` maps the account value to an Account entity (a user), and `HostCustomEntity` maps the computer value to a Host entity (a computer). The query does not map an IP-address or resource-group entity. [Map data fields to Microsoft Sentinel entities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/map-data-fields-to-entities)

You have an Azure subscription with Microsoft Defender for Cloud enhanced security features enabled, and it contains a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can export alert data from Defender for Cloud. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should be assigned to User1?
questions.explanation:
The Azure Reader role grants read-only access to Defender for Cloud alerts and related security information, which is sufficient to export alert data. Contributor and Owner add write or administrative capabilities that are unnecessary, and User Access Administrator is intended for managing access assignments.

**Learn more:** [User roles and permissions - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/permissions) · [Download a CSV report - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/export-alerts-to-csv)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are configuring Microsoft Cloud App Security.  
  
You have a custom threat-detection policy based on the IP address ranges for your company's United States-based offices.  
  
You receive many alerts related to impossible travel and sign-ins from risky IP addresses. You determine that 99% of the alerts are legitimate sign-ins from your corporate offices.  
  
You need to prevent alerts for legitimate sign-ins from known locations.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Add the IP addresses to the corporate address range category.
Increase the sensitivity level of the impossible travel anomaly detection policy.
Add the IP addresses to the other address range category and add a tag.
Create an activity policy that has an exclusion for the IP addresses.

questions.explanation: Adding corporate IP addresses to the **Corporate** address range category (B) automatically marks them as trusted and excludes them from risky IP detection policies. Configuring automatic data enrichment (A) allows overriding location information for known office ranges. Together, these prevent alerts on legitimate corporate traffic. Increasing sensitivity (C) would generate more alerts, not fewer. The "Other" category (D) with tags is less direct than using the designated Corporate category.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud and includes a resource group named RG1. RG1 contains 20 virtual machines running Windows Server 2019.  
  
You need to configure just-in-time (JIT) access for the virtual machines in RG1. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Limit the maximum request duration to two hours.  
- Restrict protocol access to Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) only.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud just-in-time VM access can define a per-port policy that specifies the protocol and maximum request time. Azure Policy can deploy and enforce that JIT configuration consistently across the virtual machines in a resource group, minimizing per-VM administrative work. RDP can be restricted to its TCP management port with a two-hour maximum access window.

**Learn more:** [Enable just-in-time access - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/just-in-time-access-usage) · [Enable and enforce just-in-time VM access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/enable-enforce-just-in-time-vm-access/)

Which anomaly detection policy should you use?

questions.question:

You identify eight alerts in the incident that need additional investigation.  
  
You must escalate the alerts to another Azure Sentinel administrator.  
  
What should you do to provide the alerts to that administrator?
