lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have access to a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.  
  
You are investigating a multistage security attack in your environment.  
  
You need to identify the MITRE ATT&CK phases for the tactics and techniques the attacker used. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From Microsoft Sentinel in the Microsoft Defender portal, select Threat management, an then use the MITRE ATT&CK node.
Use the Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit
From Investigation & response in the Microsoft Defender portal, select Incident & alerts, and then use the Incidents node.
From Microsoft Sentinel in the Microsoft Defender portal, select Threat management, and then use the Hunting node.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel’s MITRE ATT&CK page organizes and visualizes workspace detection coverage according to the MITRE ATT&CK tactics and techniques. In the Microsoft Defender portal, it is available at **Microsoft Sentinel > Threat management > MITRE ATT&CK**, making it the direct option with minimal administrative effort.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Sentinel in the Microsoft Defender portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/microsoft-sentinel-defender-portal) · [Understand security coverage by the MITRE ATT&CK framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/mitre-coverage)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel playbook triggered by using the Azure Activity connector.  
  
You need to create a new near-real-time (NRT) analytics rule that will use the playbook.  
  
What should you configure for the rule?
questions.explanation:
An NRT rule produces an alert directly rather than an incident, so a playbook is attached to it through the rule's alert automation settings, which run the chosen playbook whenever the NRT rule generates an alert. Incident automation settings apply only after an incident is created, and entity mapping or the query logic itself have no bearing on which playbook is invoked.\
\
**Learn more:** [Work with near-real-time (NRT) detection analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-nrt-rules)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription containing 1,000 Windows 10 devices. Microsoft Office 365 is installed on the devices.  
  
You need to mitigate these device threats:  
  
- Microsoft Excel macros that download scripts from untrusted websites  
- Users opening executable attachments in Microsoft Outlook  
- Exploits involving Outlook rules and forms  
  
What should you use?

options.text: attack surface reduction rules in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
adaptive application control in Azure Defender

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint attack surface reduction rules can block Office apps and macros from creating child processes or executable content, block executable content from email clients and webmail, and block Office communication applications from creating child processes. These rules mitigate the specified Excel and Outlook attack techniques.

**Learn more:** [Attack surface reduction rules deployment overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-deployment) · [Attack surface reduction rules reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference)

/>","className":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named Workspace1 that includes the AzureActivity table.

- Minimize retention costs.  
  
To what value should you configure the retention period? Select the appropriate options in the answer area.

questions.explanation:
AzureActivity data is retained for at least 90 days at no charge, and it is available for interactive queries during analytics retention. Solution: From **Entity tags**, you add the accounts as Honeytoken accounts.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Identity supports manually applying the Honeytoken tag to user accounts. Honeytoken accounts act as traps for malicious actors; authentication involving one typically generates an alert.\
\
**Learn more:** [Defender for Identity entity tags in Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-for-identity/entity-tags)

questions.question:
Solution: In Azure AD Identity Protection, you configure the sign-in risk policy.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Accounts intended as traps for malicious actors must be configured as honeytoken accounts in Microsoft Defender for Identity. A sign-in risk policy in Azure AD Identity Protection evaluates and remediates risky sign-ins, not honeytoken-account configuration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Entity tags in Microsoft Defender for Identity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-for-identity/entity-tags)

questions.question:
Solution: You add the accounts to an Active Directory group, then add that group as a Sensitive group.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Honeytoken accounts must be tagged as Honeytoken to serve as traps for malicious actors; authentication associated with a honeytoken account triggers an alert. A Sensitive tag is used for detections that depend on an entity’s sensitivity status and does not configure accounts as honeytokens.\
\
**Learn more:** [Defender for Identity entity tags in Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-for-identity/entity-tags)

questions.question:
Solution: You add each account as a Sensitive account.  
  
Does this fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Identity uses honeytoken accounts as traps for malicious actors; authentication to a normally dormant honeytoken account triggers an alert. The Sensitive tag instead identifies high-value entities and enables detections that depend on an entity’s sensitivity status, so it does not create attacker-decoy accounts.\
\
**Learn more:** [Defender for Identity entity tags in Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-for-identity/entity-tags)

questions.question:
Solution: You add each account as a Sensitive account.  
  
Does this fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation:
Fusion is Microsoft Sentinel’s built-in correlation engine and analytics rule type for automatically detecting advanced multistage attacks. It correlates anomalous behaviors and suspicious activities across stages of an attack and generates incidents comprising two or more alerts or activities. Fusion is enabled by default, so it requires minimal administration.

**Learn more:** [Advanced multistage attack detection in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/fusion) · [Configure multistage attack detection (Fusion) rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/configure-fusion-rules)

questions.question:

Modify the properties of the computer objects listed as exposed entities.

You have a virtual machine running Windows 10 with the Log Analytics agent installed.

questions.question:

You need to implement deception rules. The solution must ensure that you can limit the scope of the rules.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation: Device tags must be created first to scope deception rules to specific devices. Deception rule configuration allows scoping via 'Devices with specific tags,' providing granular control over which devices host deception lures. Device groups, while useful for organization, cannot directly scope deception rule deployment. Honeytoken and sensitive entity tags serve different purposes in threat intelligence management.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
You need to implement deception rules. The solution must ensure that you can limit the scope of the rules.  
  
What should you create first?

options.text: Modify the access control settings for the key vault.
Modify the access policy for the key vault.

questions.explanation:
The Key Vault firewall can deny data-plane access by default and permit only approved public IP ranges or virtual networks. This promptly blocks suspicious IP addresses while legitimate users can retain access through configured allow rules. Access policies and access-control settings govern authorized identities, not the source-network boundary.

**Learn more:** [Configure network security for Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/network-security) · [Virtual network service endpoints for Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/overview-vnet-service-endpoints)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.  
  
You receive multiple alerts for failed sign-in attempts against an account.  
  
You determine that the alerts are false positives.  
  
You need to stop any additional failed sign-in alerts from being generated for the account. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Ensure failed sign-in alerts continue to be generated for other accounts.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add an activity template to the entity behavior.

questions.explanation:
An analytics rule determines whether failed sign-in alerts are generated. Modify its query or filtering logic to exclude the identified account; this suppresses future alerts for that account while preserving the rule’s detections for all other accounts. Automation rules run only after alerts or incidents are created, so they cannot prevent the alerts themselves.

**Learn more:** [Create and use Microsoft Sentinel automation rules to manage response](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-manage-use-automation-rules) · [Scheduled analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/scheduled-rules-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 tenant and a known threat file named File1.docx.  
  
You need to stop users from downloading File1.docx.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Defender portal, add an indicator.
From the Microsoft Purview portal, create a data loss prevention (DLP) policy.
From the Microsoft Purview portal, create a sensitivity label.
From the Microsoft Defender portal configure an automated investigation.

questions.explanation:
A file indicator in the Microsoft Defender portal can create a block entry for the file’s SHA-256 hash, preventing the known malicious file from being delivered or accessed through the applicable Defender protection workflow. DLP policies and sensitivity labels classify or restrict sensitive data, not a known threat file, while automated investigation does not itself create the required block.

**Learn more:** [Allow or block files using the Tenant Allow/Block List](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/tenant-allow-block-list-files-configure) · [Create indicators for files](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/indicator-file)

Which JSON key should you search?

options.text: Create custom rule based on the Office 365 connector templates.
Create a Microsoft incident creation rule based on Azure Security Center.
Create a Microsoft Cloud App Security connector.
Create an Azure AD Identity Protection connector.

questions.explanation:
Fusion scenarios that correlate a suspicious Microsoft Entra ID sign-in with anomalous Microsoft 365 activity require data from both Microsoft Entra ID Protection and Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps (formerly Microsoft Cloud App Security). The Identity Protection connector supplies the suspicious-sign-in alerts, and the Cloud App Security connector supplies the anomalous cloud and Office 365 activity alerts.

**Learn more:** [Create custom detection rules in Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/custom-detection-rules)

questions.question:
Solution: Enable Azure Arc and onboard the virtual machines to Azure Arc.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Arc enables AWS virtual machines to be connected as Azure Arc-enabled servers, allowing Microsoft Defender for Cloud to deploy the required agents or extensions through auto-provisioning and monitor their security posture.\
\
**Learn more:** [Plan a Defender for Servers deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/plan-defender-for-servers) · [Connect your AWS account](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/quickstart-onboard-aws)

questions.question:
Solution: Manually install the Log Analytics agent on the virtual machines.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Log Analytics agent collects security-related configurations and event logs from virtual machines and sends the data to a Log Analytics workspace for security monitoring. Manual deployment of the agent enables that collection when automatic deployment is not used or has not completed.\
\
**Learn more:** [Reference table for all compute security recommendations in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/recommendations-reference-compute)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You have the following KQL query.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783741891335-bitlvt36.png)  
  
You need to ensure that you can create a Microsoft Defender XDR custom detection rule by using this query.  
  
What should you add to the query?

options.text: | summarize (Timestamp, ReportId)=arg_max(Timestamp, ReportId), count() by DeviceId
| summarize (Timestamp, DeviceName)=arg_min(Timestamp, DeviceName), count() by DeviceId

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Defender for Endpoint custom detection query must return `Timestamp`, `DeviceId`, and `ReportId` from the same event. Grouping by `DeviceId` retains that identifier, while `arg_max(Timestamp, ReportId)` returns the latest event timestamp and its matching report ID. Microsoft documents this exact aggregation pattern for antivirus-detection queries.

**Learn more:** [Create custom detection rules in Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/custom-detection-rules)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Sentinel.  
  
You need to reduce the administrative effort needed to respond to incidents and remediate security threats detected by Microsoft Sentinel.  
  
Which two features should you use? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel automation rules centrally manage automated incident handling and can run a playbook when defined alert or incident conditions are met. Microsoft Sentinel playbooks provide the response and remediation workflow logic, enabling automated and orchestrated actions against threats.

**Learn more:** [Automation in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/automation) · [Create and use Microsoft Sentinel automation rules to manage response](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-manage-use-automation-rules)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription containing two groups, Group1 and Group2, and it uses Microsoft Copilot for Security.  
  
You must configure Copilot for Security role assignments to meet these requirements:  
  
- Ensure that Group1 members can run prompts and respond to Microsoft Defender XDR security incidents.  
- Ensure that Group2 members can run prompts.  
- Follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
You remove Everyone from the Copilot Contributor role.  
  
Which two actions should you perform next? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Assign the Security Operator role to Group1.
Assign the Copilot Owner role to Group2.
Assign the Copilot Owner role to Group1
Assign the Security Operator role to Group2.
Assign the Copilot Contributor role to Group2.

questions.explanation:
The Security Operator role gives Group1 the Microsoft Defender XDR permissions needed to respond to security incidents and provides Security Copilot access through the recommended Microsoft security roles. The Copilot Contributor role gives Group2 access to run prompts without the tenant-wide administration privileges granted by Copilot Owner.

**Learn more:** [Understand authentication in Microsoft Security Copilot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/security/authentication) · [Microsoft Security Copilot in Microsoft Defender](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/security-copilot-in-microsoft-365-defender)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has one office in Istanbul and a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
The company intends to use Conditional Access policies to enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA).  
  
You need to require MFA for every user who works remotely.  
  
What should the solution include?
questions.explanation:
A named location defines the office network’s public IP ranges and can be marked trusted. A Conditional Access MFA policy can include any network or location while excluding that trusted office location, which requires MFA for users signing in remotely. [Microsoft Learn: Require MFA for all users with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-mfa-strength)

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Learn: Require MFA for all users with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-mfa-strength) · [Microsoft Learn: Conditional Access network assignment conditions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-assignment-network)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace with User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) enabled for Signin Logs.  
  
You need to make sure failed interactive sign-ins are detected while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation: With UEBA enabled on the Signin Logs data source, Microsoft Sentinel can apply its built-in UEBA activity templates, which already recognize and baseline events such as failed interactive sign-ins without any custom query authoring. A scheduled alert query or hunting query would instead require writing and maintaining custom KQL, and the Activity Log connector ingests Azure subscription activity rather than sign-in behavior.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace with User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) enabled for Signin Logs.  
  
You need to make sure failed interactive sign-ins are detected while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: Assign User1 a Microsoft 365 E5 license.
Assign User1 and User2 a Microsoft 365 E5 license.
Add User2 to the Audit Reader role group.
Assign User2 a Microsoft 365 E5 license.

questions.explanation:
Audit records for non-E5 users are retained for 180 days. To retain audit logs for more than 180 days and up to one year, the user who generates the audited activity must have a Microsoft 365 E5 license (or an eligible Audit Premium license). Licensing User1 therefore preserves User1’s future Exchange audit data long enough to search events that are 240 days old; licensing the searching user does not extend the retention of User1’s records.

**Learn more:** [Manage audit log retention policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-log-retention-policies) · [Search the audit log](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-search)

questions.question: Which team's issue can be resolved by using Microsoft Defender for Office 365?
questions.explanation:
The marketing team collaborates with external vendors through SharePoint Online and has experienced vendors uploading malware. Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Safe Attachments adds protection for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams by detecting and blocking malicious files in sites and document libraries, so it addresses the marketing team's issue.\
\
**Learn more:** [Safe Attachments for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/safe-attachments-for-spo-odfb-teams-about)

questions.question: Which team's issue can be resolved by using Microsoft Defender for Office 365?

options.text: Create a suppression rule scoped to any device.
Create a suppression rule scoped to a device group.

questions.explanation:
A suppression rule can hide known benign alerts from the Alerts queue. Scoping the rule to the accounting device group confines the exception to the devices that use the macro-enabled documents, while preserving alert visibility for similar activity on other devices. The false-positive alert must be generated before it can be identified and used to define the suppression rule.

**Learn more:** [Manage Microsoft Defender for Endpoint suppression rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/manage-suppression-rules) · [Investigate Microsoft Defender for Endpoint alerts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/investigate-alerts)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
You need to filter the security alerts view to display these alerts:  
  
- Unusual user accessed a key vault  
- Log on from an unusual location  
- Impossible travel activity  
  
Which severity should you select?
questions.explanation:
All three listed alert types have a Medium severity classification in Microsoft Defender for Cloud. Filtering the security alerts view by Medium includes each of them.\
\
**Learn more:** [Alerts for Azure Key Vault — Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/alerts-azure-key-vault) · [Alerts for SQL Database and Azure Synapse Analytics — Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/alerts-sql-database-and-azure-synapse-analytics)

options.text: a Log Analytics Data Collector API

questions.explanation:
The Syslog connector is designed to collect native Syslog messages from Linux virtual machines through the Azure Monitor Agent. It ingests the logs into the Syslog table without requiring a custom Data Collector API or REST integration, and avoids the extra CEF-specific formatting and parsing required when CEF is used. [Microsoft Learn: Syslog and CEF via AMA connectors](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/cef-syslog-ama-overview)

**Learn more:** [Syslog and CEF AMA connectors - Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/cef-syslog-ama-overview)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
You need to identify all the entities affected by an incident.  
  
Which tab should you use in the Microsoft Defender portal?
questions.explanation:
The Evidence and Response tab on the incident page consolidates every entity implicated in the incident's alerts, such as files, processes, users, devices, and IP addresses, together with the remediation status and available actions for each, making it the tab used to identify all entities affected by an incident.\
\
**Learn more:** [Investigate incidents in Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/investigate-incidents)

questions.question:
A company uses Azure Sentinel.  
  
You need to create an automated response to threats.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel playbooks implement automated threat-response workflows. They can run remediation or orchestration actions automatically in response to alerts and incidents.\
\
**Learn more:** [Automate threat response with playbooks in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/automate-responses-with-playbooks)

questions.question:
A company uses Azure Sentinel.  
  
You need to create an automated response to threats.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: The rule query takes too long to run and times out.
Permissions to the data sources of the rule query were modified.
There are connectivity issues between the data sources and Log Analytics

questions.explanation:
A rule query that exceeds its execution time limit can time out, and connectivity problems between data sources and Log Analytics can temporarily prevent rule execution. Microsoft Sentinel classifies both conditions as transient failures, so the rule can fail intermittently and later succeed.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshooting analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/troubleshoot-analytics-rules)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud and includes a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can modify Microsoft Defender for Cloud security policies. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation:
The Security Admin built-in role for Microsoft Defender for Cloud can update security policies while providing only Defender for Cloud security-management permissions. Owner and Contributor are broader roles, so they do not meet the least-privilege requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [User roles and permissions - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/permissions) · [Azure built-in roles for Security - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/security)

You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named Workspace1 that is connected to the Microsoft Sentinel data lake and includes a table named Table1.  
  
You need to create a scheduled KQL job named Job1 that runs every hour, queries data across multiple Microsoft Sentinel workspaces, and writes Job1 output to Table1.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Assign the Microsoft Sentinel Reader role on Workspace1 to the managed identity of Job1.
Add a project statement to Job1.
Ensure that the output of Job1 matches the schema of Table1.

questions.explanation:
When a KQL job appends results to an existing Microsoft Sentinel data lake table, its query output must match the destination table’s schema, including the column names and data types. KQL jobs support scheduled execution and a query scope of multiple workspaces.

**Learn more:** [Create KQL jobs in the Microsoft Sentinel data lake](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/datalake/kql-jobs) · [Troubleshoot KQL queries for the data lake](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/datalake/kql-troubleshoot)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are investigating a possible attack that deploys a new ransomware strain.  
  
You have three custom device groups. The groups contain devices that store highly sensitive information.  
  
You plan to perform automated actions on all devices.  
  
You need to be able to temporarily group the machines to perform actions on the devices.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Assign a tag to the device group.
Add the device users to the admin role.
Add a tag to the machines.
Create a new device group that has a rank of 1.
Create a new device group that has a rank of 4.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint device groups can define membership through tags. Apply a common tag to the machines and associate that tag with the temporary device group as its matching criterion. A device that matches more than one group is assigned only to the highest-ranked group, so assigning the temporary group rank 1 makes it take precedence during the automated-response period. Automated remediation settings are configured through device groups; creating or changing an administrator role is not needed to form this temporary device grouping.

**Learn more:** [Create and manage device groups in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/defender-endpoint/machine-groups) · [Configure automated investigation and remediation capabilities in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/configure-automated-investigations-remediation)

questions.question:
You intend to create a custom Azure Sentinel query that tracks anomalous Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) sign-in activity and displays that activity as a time chart aggregated by day.  
  
You need to create a query to display the time chart.  
  
What should you include in the query?
questions.explanation:
The Kusto `bin()` function groups datetime values into fixed intervals, such as daily (`1d`) bins. It is used with aggregation to produce daily time-series data for a time chart.\
\
**Learn more:** [bin() - Kusto | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/kusto/query/bin-function?view=microsoft-fabric)

questions.question:
You intend to create a custom Azure Sentinel query that tracks anomalous Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) sign-in activity and displays that activity as a time chart aggregated by day.  
  
You need to create a query to display the time chart.  
  
What should you include in the query?

options.text: Enable User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA).
Modify the properties of the connector.

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Sentinel scheduled query rule supports alert enrichment: fields from the query results can be surfaced as custom details and used to customize alert properties for each alert instance. This is the mechanism for controlling details included in alerts generated for selected events from connected data.

**Learn more:** [Create scheduled analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-analytics-rules) · [Customize alert details in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/customize-alert-details)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR. The subscription includes 500 devices that are joined to Microsoft Entra, belong to the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint default device group, and are managed using Microsoft Intune.  
  
You need to implement Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first in the Microsoft Defender portal?

options.text: From Configuration management, configure the Enforcement scope settings.
Configure auto remediation for the default device group.
Set Microsoft Intune connection to On.

questions.explanation:
Enabling the Microsoft Intune connection lets Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management create Intune security tasks for remediation requests on Microsoft Entra-joined, Intune-managed devices. This uses the existing Intune management relationship and avoids configuring a separate enforcement scope or unrelated response features.

**Learn more:** [Remediate vulnerabilities with Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-vulnerability-management/tvm-remediation) · [Use Intune to remediate vulnerabilities found by Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/intune-service/protect/microsoft-defender-manage-vulnerabilities)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender 365.  
  
You need to ensure you can investigate threats by using data from the unified audit log in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.  
  
What should you configure first?
questions.explanation:
The Office 365 connector connects Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps to Microsoft 365 audit data, providing visibility into audited activities for threat investigation. Microsoft documentation identifies Microsoft 365 auditing as a prerequisite for monitoring Microsoft 365 activities and describes connecting Microsoft 365 through the app connector.\
\
**Learn more:** [Protect your Microsoft 365 environment - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/protect-office-365)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender 365.  
  
You need to ensure you can investigate threats by using data from the unified audit log in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.  
  
What should you configure first?

options.text: AuditLogs -| where Timestamp between (datetime(2023-02-01)..datetime(2023-02-10))| where FileName contains “Project1”
AuditLogs -| where Timestamp > ago(10d)| where FileName contains “Project1”

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview eDiscovery content searches use KeyQL. A `c:c` expression combines the keyword and the condition with AND-like behavior, and a date range is expressed as `date=start..end`. With Team1's SharePoint team site scoped as the search location, `Project1(c:c)(date=2023-02-01..2023-02-10)` returns content matching Project1 within that date range. `AuditLogs | where ...` is Azure Monitor/Log Analytics query syntax, not Purview KeyQL.

**Learn more:** [Get started with Content search](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-in/purview/ediscovery-content-search) · [Use Keyword Query Language to create search queries in eDiscovery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/edisc-keyword-query-language)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that contains a device named Device1. Device1 is enrolled in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
Device1 reports an incident that includes a file named File1.exe as evidence.  
  
You initiate the Collect Investigation Package action and download the ZIP file.  
  
You need to identify the first and last time File1.exe was executed.  
  
What should you review in the investigation package?
questions.explanation: **Prefetch files** (.pf files) in Windows record execution metadata including the first and last execution times of applications. The operating system maintains this data to optimize startup performance. This is the forensically reliable source for execution history. Processes only show currently running applications, and event logs do not consistently capture this granular execution data.

questions.question:
You use Azure Security Center.  
  
You receive a security alert in Security Center. You need to view the recommendations for resolving the alert in Security Center.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From Security alerts, select the alert, select Take Action, and then expand the Prevent future attacks section.
From Security alerts, select Take Action, and then expand the Mitigate the threat section.
From Regulatory compliance, download the report.
From Recommendations, download the CSV report.

questions.explanation:
In a Security Center alert’s Take action pane, the Prevent future attacks section provides security recommendations that reduce attack surface and improve security posture. The Mitigate the threat section instead contains manual remediation steps for the alert.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage and respond to security alerts — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/manage-respond-alerts)

questions.question:
You use Azure Security Center.  
  
You receive a security alert in Security Center. You need to view the recommendations for resolving the alert in Security Center.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
The **Contain device** action causes every Microsoft Defender for Endpoint-onboarded device to block incoming and outgoing communication with the contained device. It is intended to stop lateral movement from a compromised or potentially compromised unmanaged device, including a Linux endpoint that is not itself onboarded.

**Learn more:** [Take response actions on a device in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/respond-machine-alerts)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named WS1.  
  
You create a hunting query that detects a new attack vector. The attack vector maps to a tactic listed in the MITRE ATT&CK database.  
  
You need to ensure that an incident is created in WS1 when the new attack vector is detected.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation: A scheduled query rule allows you to run a hunting query on a recurring basis and automatically create incidents when matches are detected. This rule type executes the query at defined intervals and triggers incident creation when the attack vector is found, enabling continuous detection without manual intervention. Hunting livestream sessions, query bookmarks, and Fusion rules serve different purposes.

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named WS1.  
  
You create a hunting query that detects a new attack vector. The attack vector maps to a tactic listed in the MITRE ATT&CK database.  
  
You need to ensure that an incident is created in WS1 when the new attack vector is detected.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: a scheduled analytics rule that queries the analytics tier only

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel KQL jobs run one-time or scheduled asynchronous KQL queries on data in the data lake tier. They are intended for investigations using historical logs and support joins or unions across multiple tables; their supported query time range is up to 12 years.

**Learn more:** [KQL jobs, summary rules, and search jobs - Microsoft Security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/datalake/kql-jobs-summary-rules-search-jobs) · [Create KQL jobs in the Microsoft Sentinel data lake](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/datalake/kql-jobs)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes 100 Linux devices. The devices are onboarded to Microsoft Defender 365.  
  
You need to start collecting investigation packages from the devices by using the Microsoft 365 Defender portal.  
  
Which response action should you use?
questions.explanation:
The **Collect investigation package** response action gathers investigation and forensic data from a supported onboarded device through the Microsoft 365 Defender portal. Linux is supported for this response action.\
\
**Learn more:** [Collect investigation package from devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/collect-investigation-package)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company uses Microsoft Sentinel to manage alerts from more than 10,000 IoT devices.  
  
A security manager reports that the high volume of incidents is making security-threat tracking increasingly difficult.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that provides a custom visualization to simplify threat investigations and enables threats to be inferred by using machine learning.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel workbooks provide customizable, interactive dashboards that consolidate log-query results, tables, and charts into a single visualization, which is exactly what's needed to simplify investigation across a high-incident-volume IoT environment. Workbooks can also surface the output of Sentinel's built-in machine-learning-based analytics (such as anomaly and Fusion detections), letting analysts infer threats visually rather than manually correlating raw alerts.

**Learn more:** [Visualize and monitor your data by using workbooks in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/monitor-your-data)

questions.question:
You need to add notes to events to satisfy the Azure Sentinel requirements.  
  
Which three actions should you carry out, in order?

/>","className":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure logic app named app1 and a Microsoft Sentinel workspace with an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) connector.  
  
You need to ensure that app1 starts when Microsoft Sentinel detects an alert generated by Azure AD.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Sentinel analytics rule evaluates connected Azure AD data and generates the alert. After that alert source exists, an automation rule can be configured with an alert-created trigger to run the Logic Apps workflow. Microsoft documents that alerts can be created by scheduled or near-real-time analytics rules, and that an automation rule using the alert trigger can run a playbook.

**Learn more:** [Create and use Microsoft Sentinel automation rules to manage response](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-manage-use-automation-rules) · [Create scheduled analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/create-analytics-rules)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Azure Defender.  
  
You have 100 virtual machines in a resource group named RG1.  
  
You assign the Security Admin role to a new user named SecAdmin1.  
  
You need to ensure that SecAdmin1 can use Azure Defender to apply quick fixes to the virtual machines. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to SecAdmin1?

options.text: the Security Reader role for the subscription

questions.explanation:
The Defender for Cloud **Fix** action for applying security recommendations requires Contributor- or Owner-level permissions at the relevant resource group or subscription scope; Security Admin alone cannot perform it. Contributor on RG1 permits remediation of the virtual machines in that resource group without granting unnecessary subscription-wide access or Owner privileges.

**Learn more:** [User roles and permissions — Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/permissions) · [Investigate the health of your resources — Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/investigate-resource-health)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 tenant that uses Microsoft Exchange Online and Microsoft Defender for Office 365.  
  
What should you use to determine whether zero-hour auto purge (ZAP) moved an email message from a user's mailbox?

options.text: the Threat Protection Status report in Microsoft Defender for Office 365
the mailbox audit log in Exchange
the Safe Attachments file types report in Microsoft Defender for Office 365
the mail flow report in Exchange

questions.explanation:
The Exchange Mailflow status report includes a Mailflow view that shows ZAP-affected messages for a selected date range. ZAP actions are not recorded as system actions in Exchange mailbox audit logs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Zero-hour auto purge in Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/zero-hour-auto-purge)

You are configuring Azure Sentinel.  
  
You need to send a Microsoft Teams message to a channel whenever an incident that represents a sign-in risk event becomes active in Azure Sentinel.  
  
Which two actions should you take in Azure Sentinel? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Associate a playbook to the analytics rule that triggered the incident.

questions.explanation:
A playbook is the Logic Apps-based automation that can post a message to a Microsoft Teams channel, so it must first be created (Add a playbook) and then associated with the analytics rule that generates the sign-in-risk incident so it runs automatically whenever that incident is triggered. Entity behavior analytics, the Fusion rule, and a workbook do not send notifications and play no role in triggering a Teams message.

**Learn more:** [Automate threat response with playbooks in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/automation/automate-responses-with-playbooks)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.  
  
You have a query named Query1, shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783732853918-r3gojnn7.png)  
  
You plan to create a custom parser named Parser1.  
  
You need to use Query1 in Parser1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: In line 3, replace the !contains operator with the !has operator.
In line 4, remove the TimeGenerated predicate.

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Sentinel parser should not filter records by time, because the query that uses the parser applies the time range. Removing the `TimeGenerated > ago(7h)` filter prevents Parser1 from being restricted to only the preceding seven hours.\
\
**Learn more:** [Develop Microsoft Sentinel ASIM parsers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/normalization-develop-parsers)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender XDR.  
  
You are investigating an incident.  
  
You need to review the incident tasks that were performed. The solution must include a query that will display the incidents in a workbook, and then display the tasks of each incident in another grid.  
  
Which table should you target in the query?
questions.explanation: The SecurityIncident table in Kusto Query Language (used by Sentinel workbooks) contains incident metadata including incident ID, severity, status, and task information. Querying this table allows you to display incidents in one grid and detail their associated tasks in another grid. SecurityEvent, SentinelAudit, and SecurityAlert tables do not contain incident task details.

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783735829239-hhw0nn5t.png)  
  
You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
You need to enable Microsoft Defender for Servers on every resource.  
  
Which resources require installation of the Azure Arc agent?
questions.explanation:
Azure Arc-enabled servers uses the Connected Machine agent to onboard servers hosted on-premises or in another cloud to Azure. Therefore, the on-premises servers and the AWS virtual machine require the agent. An Azure virtual machine already has native Azure management capabilities and does not require Azure Arc.

**Learn more:** [Select a Defender for Servers plan - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/plan-defender-for-servers-select-plan) · [Azure Arc-enabled servers overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-arc/servers/overview)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Security Copilot.  
  
You have the files listed in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783746021772-8w3c25xu.png)  
  
Each file contains a copy of your company's compliance policy.  
  
You need to ensure that Security Copilot responses are informed by the compliance policy.  
  
Which files can you upload to Security Copilot?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Security Copilot supports DOCX, PDF, and TXT uploads when each individual file is no larger than 3 MB. The 2-MB PDF and 128-KB TXT file meet those requirements; the 4-MB DOCX file does not.\
\
**Learn more:** [Upload a file in Microsoft Security Copilot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/security/upload-file)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft 365 Defender and has data loss prevention (DLP) policies configured with aggregated alerts.  
  
You need to identify the entities affected by an aggregated alert.  
  
What should you review in the DLP alert management dashboard in the Microsoft 365 compliance center?

options.text: the Events tab of the alert
the Sensitive Info Types tab of the alert
the Details tab of the alert

questions.explanation:
Aggregated DLP alerts group multiple policy-match events. The Events tab shows the events included in the alert, and each event’s details include affected entities such as the user, device, IP address, and file information.\
\
**Learn more:** [Get started with data loss prevention alerts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-alerts-get-started) · [Get started with the DLP Alerts dashboard](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-alerts-dashboard-get-started)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription and a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.  
  
You need to create a KQL query that combines data from these sources:  
  
- Microsoft Graph  
- Risky users detected by using Microsoft Entra ID Protection  
  
The solution must minimize the amount of data returned.  
  
How should the query begin?
questions.explanation:
`join` defaults to the `innerunique` join flavor, which returns only records from `MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs` that have a matching `AADRiskyUsers` record and deduplicates the left side. This avoids returning unrelated Microsoft Graph activity records, unlike a `leftouter` lookup, which retains all left-side rows.

**Learn more:** [join operator - Kusto | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/kusto/query/join-operator?view=azure-monitor)
